MAPPING: Taps in every my_fir_* module are d0=din, d1..d6=n_delay_reg1..n_delay_reg6, all 16 bits unsigned. Every filter is symmetric in the source (C6==C0, C5==C1, C4==C2 in each module's define block), so equal-coefficient taps are pre-added in soft logic at 17 bits and one 17-bit sum drives one 18-bit operand port; each block then carries two coefficient groups instead of one, which is what cuts the block count from 144 to 84 and the post-adder tree from two levels to one. Coefficients are taken from the module's own define through a 19-bit localparam (do not retype the numbers): localparam [18:0] C0 = COEF0_b;` and so on, one per coefficient the module uses.

Seven-tap modules (my_fir_f1 with 29,101,15,235,15,101,29; my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2 with 4,42,163,255,163,42,4) get three pre-adds and two blocks:
wire [16:0] s0 = din + n_delay_reg6;
wire [16:0] s1 = n_delay_reg1 + n_delay_reg5;
wire [16:0] s2 = n_delay_reg2 + n_delay_reg4;
sop0: ax={1'b0,s0}, ay=C0, bx={1'b0,s1}, by=C1
sop1: ax={1'b0,s2}, ay=C2, bx={2'b0,n_delay_reg3}, by=C3
dout <= sop0[27:0] + sop1[27:0];

Six-tap modules (my_fir_f3 with 12,77,148,-,148,77,12; my_fir_h1 with 15,25,193,-,193,25,15; my_fir_h3 and my_fir_h4 with 9,56,109,-,109,56,9) get two pre-adds and two blocks; din is deliberately left un-pre-added, so the module input, the latest-arriving operand, reaches its block with no soft cell in front of it:
wire [16:0] s1 = n_delay_reg1 + n_delay_reg5;
wire [16:0] s2 = n_delay_reg2 + n_delay_reg4;
sop0: ax={2'b0,din}, ay=C0, bx={2'b0,n_delay_reg6}, by=C6
sop1: ax={1'b0,s1}, ay=C1, bx={1'b0,s2}, by=C2
dout <= sop0[27:0] + sop1[27:0];

Every input port of every block is connected; the only unused product term is sop1.bx/by in no module (all four ports carry real terms everywhere), so no port is tied to 0 in this rewrite. Each block's result is read as result[27:0]; the two are added at 28 bits and assigned to the existing dout register inside the existing if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) branch, so the enable and output_data_ready are untouched.

PLAN:

Converted: all 45 candidate ids in the seven my_fir_* modules (6 instances each, 270 products in all). Left: all 45 fltr_compute_* candidates, for one shared reason. In fltr_compute_f1/f2/f3/h1/h2/h3/h4 each product is registered into a 17-bit q and the sum adds {q[16],q[16],q[16],q} (lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), i.e. each product is sign-extended from bit 16 before being summed. In fltr_compute_f1 (coefficient 9'b100010101 = 277), f3 (9'b101101100 = 364) and h4 (9'b101000100 = 324) a product can reach 70635, 92820, 82620, so q[16] is really set for some inputs and the sum is not the sum of the true products; two such products cannot share a block, because the block returns only p_a+p_b and the correction needs p_a[16] and p_b[16] separately. In the other four the sign bit is always 0, but converting them would still cost 2 tiles per module instance against the 7/4 of a tile they hold today in mult_9x9_fixed_pt mode (four to a tile), and it would have to replace the seven q registers with new registers whose initial value the contract leaves unknown while the originals start at 0. Both ways it loses, so every fltr_compute product stays as it is.

Blocks and tiles: 14 blocks per instance set (2 in each of the seven my_fir_* modules) x 6 instances = 84 blocks, 60 fewer than the kept 144. Each takes a DSP tile alone, so the design uses 84 + the 59 tiles that hold the untouched fltr_compute mult_9x9 products = 143 tiles, against 203 measured for the kept candidate and 224 for the baseline. That removes about 1.52e7 of tile area; the soft logic moves the other way by only about 54 cells across the whole design (per instance set: seven 28-bit post-adders stay, 10 are deleted, 17 pre-adders of 17 bits are added), so used logic area should fall from 8.66e7 to roughly 7.2e7.

Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. No block feeds another; every block's result goes straight into the single 28-bit soft adder in front of dout. That series is 2.14 ns of the stage.

Slowest stage the rewrite leaves, and what soft logic leaves it: the stage is still register -> dout, the same one the kept candidate's 8.05107 ns path runs through. In the kept candidate that stage is block -> 28-bit adder (22 carry stages, 0.960 wire + 0.622) -> 28-bit adder (1.000 wire + 0.069) -> enable-mux LUT (1.389 wire + 0.153). One whole 28-bit adder level leaves the stage in every my_fir_* module, replaced in the seven-tap modules by one 17-bit pre-adder level ahead of the block and in the six-tap modules by a pre-adder level that din, the module input and the latest operand, does not pass through at all. Estimated worst path, a seven-tap module where din does go through the pre-add: 0.060 clock-to-output + 1.419 wire to the pre-adder + about 1.069 for the pre-adder and its wire + 2.140 block + 0.960 wire + 0.622 for the 28-bit carry chain + 1.389 wire + 0.153 enable LUT + 0.019 setup = about 7.83 ns; the six-tap modules' din path drops to about 6.8 ns and their pre-added paths to about 7.8 ns. The pre-add level and the deleted post-add level are near enough the same cost (median soft adder level 1.069 ns including its wire) that this stage is expected to come out between the kept 8.05 and about 8.5 ns in the worst case; the area and wirelength it buys are worth that risk, since 60 DSP tiles is about 17% of the used logic area. STAGE_NS is given as 7.9 for the rewritten stage. The fltr_compute d_out_tmp stage (q registers through six 20-bit adder levels) is untouched and measured no worse than 8.05 ns at seed 1, so it, not this rewrite, may set the period if the rewritten stage lands below it; that is the reason the delay gain is claimed small while the area gain is claimed large.

Register stages, per converted region, before and after: unchanged everywhere. Before, each product tap * COEF is combinational from the tap registers (din from the driving fltr_compute dout register through h_fltr, n_delay_reg1..6 from the module's own shift chain; the candidate table records 0 register stages between the products and the sum) and the whole sum is latched by dout under new_data_rdy. After, the pre-add, the two blocks and the one 28-bit adder are all combinational in that same stage and the same dout register latches the result under the same enable: still 0 register stages between a product and its sum, and the same single register boundary at dout. No register is added, moved or removed, so nothing depends on the initial value of a new register and the shift chain, output_data_ready and every module port keep their exact behaviour.

Equivalence: all operands are unsigned 16-bit taps and all coefficients are positive (the negative variants in the source are commented out, e.g. lines 1442-1447, 1558-1567, 1617-1624, 1731-1740, 1789-1798), so a pair sum is 17 bits, each block product is at most (2^17-1)*255 < 2^37 and each block's two-product sum is exact at 64 bits. Per module the total is at most 65535 * (sum of coefficients) = at most 65535*673 < 2^26 for f2/h2 and less elsewhere, so taking result[27:0] from each block and adding at 28 bits reproduces the original 28-bit dout bit for bit, with no truncation and no wrap. The pre-added pairs are exactly the equal-coefficient pairs, verified per module against its `define block. No ASSUMES is needed.

DESIGN_CHANGE: in fltr_compute_f1/f3/h4 the 17-bit q registers overflow into bit 16 for large inputs (products up to 92820) and the sum then sign-extends that bit, so those filters already compute something other than their intended sum; if q were widened to 18 bits (or the products summed unsigned), the fltr_compute products could be pre-added by symmetry and folded onto this block the same way as the my_fir ones, and the six-level 20-bit adder chain behind d_out_tmp would collapse to one level.

1	// comb_sop_2_18: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx*by, all four operands unsigned
2	// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); each 18x19 product is 37
3	// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
4	// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
5	// Ports: ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every
6	// input reaches result in the same cycle.
7	module comb_sop_2_18 (
8	    input  [17:0] ax,
9	    input  [18:0] ay,
10	    input  [17:0] bx,
11	    input  [18:0] by,
12	    output [63:0] result
13	);
14	
15	    wire [36:0] prod_a = ax * ay;                                    // 18x19 -> 37, exact
16	    wire [36:0] prod_b = bx * by;                                    // 18x19 -> 37, exact
17	    wire [63:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b;                            // zero-extended, exact
18	
19	    assign result = sum;
20	
21	endmodule

PLAN:

Converted: all 45 candidate ids in the seven my_fir_* modules (6 instances each, 270 products in all). Left: all 45 fltr_compute_* candidates, for one shared reason. In fltr_compute_f1/f2/f3/h1/h2/h3/h4 each product is registered into a 17-bit q and the sum adds {q[16],q[16],q[16],q} (lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), i.e. each product is sign-extended from bit 16 before being summed. In fltr_compute_f1 (coefficient 9'b100010101 = 277), f3 (9'b101101100 = 364) and h4 (9'b101000100 = 324) a product can reach 70635, 92820, 82620, so q[16] is really set for some inputs and the sum is not the sum of the true products; two such products cannot share a block, because the block returns only p_a+p_b and the correction needs p_a[16] and p_b[16] separately. In the other four the sign bit is always 0, but converting them would still cost 2 tiles per module instance against the 7/4 of a tile they hold today in mult_9x9_fixed_pt mode (four to a tile), and it would have to replace the seven q registers with new registers whose initial value the contract leaves unknown while the originals start at 0. Both ways it loses, so every fltr_compute product stays as it is.

Blocks and tiles: 14 blocks per instance set (2 in each of the seven my_fir_* modules) x 6 instances = 84 blocks, 60 fewer than the kept 144. Each takes a DSP tile alone, so the design uses 84 + the 59 tiles that hold the untouched fltr_compute mult_9x9 products = 143 tiles, against 203 measured for the kept candidate and 224 for the baseline. That removes about 1.52e7 of tile area; the soft logic moves the other way by only about 54 cells across the whole design (per instance set: seven 28-bit post-adders stay, 10 are deleted, 17 pre-adders of 17 bits are added), so used logic area should fall from 8.66e7 to roughly 7.2e7.

Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. No block feeds another; every block's result goes straight into the single 28-bit soft adder in front of dout. That series is 2.14 ns of the stage.

Slowest stage the rewrite leaves, and what soft logic leaves it: the stage is still register -> dout, the same one the kept candidate's 8.05107 ns path runs through. In the kept candidate that stage is block -> 28-bit adder (22 carry stages, 0.960 wire + 0.622) -> 28-bit adder (1.000 wire + 0.069) -> enable-mux LUT (1.389 wire + 0.153). One whole 28-bit adder level leaves the stage in every my_fir_* module, replaced in the seven-tap modules by one 17-bit pre-adder level ahead of the block and in the six-tap modules by a pre-adder level that din, the module input and the latest operand, does not pass through at all. Estimated worst path, a seven-tap module where din does go through the pre-add: 0.060 clock-to-output + 1.419 wire to the pre-adder + about 1.069 for the pre-adder and its wire + 2.140 block + 0.960 wire + 0.622 for the 28-bit carry chain + 1.389 wire + 0.153 enable LUT + 0.019 setup = about 7.83 ns; the six-tap modules' din path drops to about 6.8 ns and their pre-added paths to about 7.8 ns. The pre-add level and the deleted post-add level are near enough the same cost (median soft adder level 1.069 ns including its wire) that this stage is expected to come out between the kept 8.05 and about 8.5 ns in the worst case; the area and wirelength it buys are worth that risk, since 60 DSP tiles is about 17% of the used logic area. STAGE_NS is given as 7.9 for the rewritten stage. The fltr_compute d_out_tmp stage (q registers through six 20-bit adder levels) is untouched and measured no worse than 8.05 ns at seed 1, so it, not this rewrite, may set the period if the rewritten stage lands below it; that is the reason the delay gain is claimed small while the area gain is claimed large.

Register stages, per converted region, before and after: unchanged everywhere. Before, each product tap * COEF is combinational from the tap registers (din from the driving fltr_compute dout register through h_fltr, n_delay_reg1..6 from the module's own shift chain; the candidate table records 0 register stages between the products and the sum) and the whole sum is latched by dout under new_data_rdy. After, the pre-add, the two blocks and the one 28-bit adder are all combinational in that same stage and the same dout register latches the result under the same enable: still 0 register stages between a product and its sum, and the same single register boundary at dout. No register is added, moved or removed, so nothing depends on the initial value of a new register and the shift chain, output_data_ready and every module port keep their exact behaviour.

Equivalence: all operands are unsigned 16-bit taps and all coefficients are positive (the negative variants in the source are commented out, e.g. lines 1442-1447, 1558-1567, 1617-1624, 1731-1740, 1789-1798), so a pair sum is 17 bits, each block product is at most (2^17-1)*255 < 2^37 and each block's two-product sum is exact at 64 bits. Per module the total is at most 65535 * (sum of coefficients) = at most 65535*673 < 2^26 for f2/h2 and less elsewhere, so taking result[27:0] from each block and adding at 28 bits reproduces the original 28-bit dout bit for bit, with no truncation and no wrap. The pre-added pairs are exactly the equal-coefficient pairs, verified per module against its `define block. No ASSUMES is needed.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Inner-loop check: the front end of the real flow, then a cell census. NOT place-and-route.
# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
# Reads, in the flow's order: blocks.vlib (every hard block of the architecture, declared from its
# models), primitives.vlib (the flow's library of memories, adders and multipliers), then the design;
# then elaborates with the flow's hierarchy check. A module that is not defined, a port name the
# block does not have, or a misspelled block name fails here as it would in the flow. Do not
# declare the target block in the design: blocks.vlib declares it, and a design that defines a module
# of the target block's name fails this check.
# Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole design (the last "Number of cells"
# table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub, registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as
# $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated module by name, which is where a hard-block
# instantiation shows up with its instance count.
set -u
f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
lib=""
[ -f "$here/blocks.vlib" ] && lib="read_verilog -lib $here/blocks.vlib; "
[ -f "$here/primitives.vlib" ] && lib="${lib}read_verilog -nomem2reg $here/primitives.vlib; "
target="$(sed -n 's|^// target block: *\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*\).*|\1|p' "$here/blocks.vlib" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
if [ -n "$target" ] && grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*module[[:space:]]+$target([^A-Za-z0-9_$]|$)" "$f"; then
  echo "FAIL: $f defines module $target; blocks.vlib declares it. Remove the module definition and keep the instances."
  exit 1
fi
out="$(yosys -p "${lib}read_verilog -sv -nolatches $f; hierarchy -check -auto-top -purge_lib; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
  echo "$out" | tail -10
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
                   on {on=0}
                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true

// comb_sop_2_18: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx*by, all four operands unsigned
// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); each 18x19 product is 37
// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
// Ports: ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every
// input reaches result in the same cycle.
module comb_sop_2_18 (
    input  [17:0] ax,
    input  [18:0] ay,
    input  [17:0] bx,
    input  [18:0] by,
    output [63:0] result
);

    wire [36:0] prod_a = ax * ay;                                    // 18x19 -> 37, exact
    wire [36:0] prod_b = bx * by;                                    // 18x19 -> 37, exact
    wire [63:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b;                            // zero-extended, exact

    assign result = sum;

endmodule

Coefficients are taken from the module's own define through a 19-bit localparam (do not retype the numbers): localparam [18:0] C0 = COEF0_b;` and so on, one per coefficient the module uses.

wire [16:0] s1 = n_delay_reg1 + n_delay_reg5;
wire [16:0] s2 = n_delay_reg2 + n_delay_reg4;
sop0: ax={2'b0,din}, ay=C0, bx={2'b0,n_delay_reg6}, by=C6
sop1: ax={1'b0,s1}, ay=C1, bx={1'b0,s2}, by=C2
dout <= sop0[27:0] + sop1[27:0];

Every input port of every block is connected; the only unused product term is sop1.bx/by in no module (all four ports carry real terms everywhere), so no port is tied to 0 in this rewrite. Each block's result is read as result[27:0]; the two are added at 28 bits and assigned to the existing dout register inside the existing if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) branch, so the enable and output_data_ready are untouched.

PLAN:

Converted: all 45 candidate ids in the seven my_fir_* modules (6 instances each, 270 products in all). Left: all 45 fltr_compute_* candidates, for one shared reason. In fltr_compute_f1/f2/f3/h1/h2/h3/h4 each product is registered into a 17-bit q and the sum adds {q[16],q[16],q[16],q} (lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), i.e. each product is sign-extended from bit 16 before being summed. In fltr_compute_f1 (coefficient 9'b100010101 = 277), f3 (9'b101101100 = 364) and h4 (9'b101000100 = 324) a product can reach 70635, 92820, 82620, so q[16] is really set for some inputs and the sum is not the sum of the true products; two such products cannot share a block, because the block returns only p_a+p_b and the correction needs p_a[16] and p_b[16] separately. In the other four the sign bit is always 0, but converting them would still cost 2 tiles per module instance against the 7/4 of a tile they hold today in mult_9x9_fixed_pt mode (four to a tile), and it would have to replace the seven q registers with new registers whose initial value the contract leaves unknown while the originals start at 0. Both ways it loses, so every fltr_compute product stays as it is.

Blocks and tiles: 14 blocks per instance set (2 in each of the seven my_fir_* modules) x 6 instances = 84 blocks, 60 fewer than the kept 144. Each takes a DSP tile alone, so the design uses 84 + the 59 tiles that hold the untouched fltr_compute mult_9x9 products = 143 tiles, against 203 measured for the kept candidate and 224 for the baseline. That removes about 1.52e7 of tile area; the soft logic moves the other way by only about 54 cells across the whole design (per instance set: seven 28-bit post-adders stay, 10 are deleted, 17 pre-adders of 17 bits are added), so used logic area should fall from 8.66e7 to roughly 7.2e7.

Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. No block feeds another; every block's result goes straight into the single 28-bit soft adder in front of dout. That series is 2.14 ns of the stage.

Slowest stage the rewrite leaves, and what soft logic leaves it: the stage is still register -> dout, the same one the kept candidate's 8.05107 ns path runs through. In the kept candidate that stage is block -> 28-bit adder (22 carry stages, 0.960 wire + 0.622) -> 28-bit adder (1.000 wire + 0.069) -> enable-mux LUT (1.389 wire + 0.153). One whole 28-bit adder level leaves the stage in every my_fir_* module, replaced in the seven-tap modules by one 17-bit pre-adder level ahead of the block and in the six-tap modules by a pre-adder level that din, the module input and the latest operand, does not pass through at all. Estimated worst path, a seven-tap module where din does go through the pre-add: 0.060 clock-to-output + 1.419 wire to the pre-adder + about 1.069 for the pre-adder and its wire + 2.140 block + 0.960 wire + 0.622 for the 28-bit carry chain + 1.389 wire + 0.153 enable LUT + 0.019 setup = about 7.83 ns; the six-tap modules' din path drops to about 6.8 ns and their pre-added paths to about 7.8 ns. The pre-add level and the deleted post-add level are near enough the same cost (median soft adder level 1.069 ns including its wire) that this stage is expected to come out between the kept 8.05 and about 8.5 ns in the worst case; the area and wirelength it buys are worth that risk, since 60 DSP tiles is about 17% of the used logic area. STAGE_NS is given as 7.9 for the rewritten stage. The fltr_compute d_out_tmp stage (q registers through six 20-bit adder levels) is untouched and measured no worse than 8.05 ns at seed 1, so it, not this rewrite, may set the period if the rewritten stage lands below it; that is the reason the delay gain is claimed small while the area gain is claimed large.

Register stages, per converted region, before and after: unchanged everywhere. Before, each product tap * COEF is combinational from the tap registers (din from the driving fltr_compute dout register through h_fltr, n_delay_reg1..6 from the module's own shift chain; the candidate table records 0 register stages between the products and the sum) and the whole sum is latched by dout under new_data_rdy. After, the pre-add, the two blocks and the one 28-bit adder are all combinational in that same stage and the same dout register latches the result under the same enable: still 0 register stages between a product and its sum, and the same single register boundary at dout. No register is added, moved or removed, so nothing depends on the initial value of a new register and the shift chain, output_data_ready and every module port keep their exact behaviour.

Equivalence: all operands are unsigned 16-bit taps and all coefficients are positive (the negative variants in the source are commented out, e.g. lines 1442-1447, 1558-1567, 1617-1624, 1731-1740, 1789-1798), so a pair sum is 17 bits, each block product is at most (2^17-1)*255 < 2^37 and each block's two-product sum is exact at 64 bits. Per module the total is at most 65535 * (sum of coefficients) = at most 65535*673 < 2^26 for f2/h2 and less elsewhere, so taking result[27:0] from each block and adding at 28 bits reproduces the original 28-bit dout bit for bit, with no truncation and no wrap. The pre-added pairs are exactly the equal-coefficient pairs, verified per module against its `define block. No ASSUMES is needed.

DESIGN_CHANGE: in fltr_compute_f1/f3/h4 the 17-bit q registers overflow into bit 16 for large inputs (products up to 92820) and the sum then sign-extends that bit, so those filters already compute something other than their intended sum; if q were widened to 18 bits (or the products summed unsigned), the fltr_compute products could be pre-added by symmetry and folded onto this block the same way as the my_fir ones, and the six-level 20-bit adder chain behind d_out_tmp would collapse to one level.

1	// comb_sop_2_18: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx*by, all four operands unsigned
2	// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); each 18x19 product is 37
3	// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
4	// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
5	// Ports: ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every
6	// input reaches result in the same cycle.
7	module comb_sop_2_18 (
8	    input  [17:0] ax,
9	    input  [18:0] ay,
10	    input  [17:0] bx,
11	    input  [18:0] by,
12	    output [63:0] result
13	);
14	
15	    wire [36:0] prod_a = ax * ay;                                    // 18x19 -> 37, exact
16	    wire [36:0] prod_b = bx * by;                                    // 18x19 -> 37, exact
17	    wire [63:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b;                            // zero-extended, exact
18	
19	    assign result = sum;
20	
21	endmodule

Task

You are the planner. Read the design source, stereovision2.v, and decide which of the candidate arithmetic regions listed below to rewrite onto the hard block described next, or that none should be rewritten. Write a plan for the editor, who carries it out; do not edit any file.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: comb_sop_2_18 (precision INT19)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx*by
  • input ports: ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19]
  • output ports: result[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and result is valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0.
The design

Baseline: the unmodified stereovision2 under this run's VPR settings (channel width 300, median of five seeds, 1 to 5) has a worst register-to-register path of 11.6069 ns on its one clock tm3_clk_v0 (I/O pads not timed) and uses 224 DSP tiles (as packed at seed 1) of the device's 306. Its used logic-block area is 9.73358e+07 minimum-width transistor areas (one DSP tile 253779, one cluster 27905) and its routed wirelength is 436921, so its area x delay x wirelength product, the objective, is 4.93619e+14. Its slowest stage (read off the seed-1 timing report) is in my_fir_f1: one hard multiply on a DSP tile (two_mult_18x19), then six adder levels with their carry chains, then one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop. The next slowest stage (read off the seed-1 timing report), in my_fir_f2 (endpoint group $dffe~642, not path 1's $dffe~456), is the same shape as path 1, one hard multiply on a DSP tile, six adder levels with their carry chains, one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop, 11.293 ns, so shortening the slowest stage past that point buys nothing on its own. Any path your rewrite creates is compared against that critical path.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Cost (guidance: go against it only with a reason in the plan)
  • The clock period is the delay of the slowest stage (the logic between one register and the next). A rewrite that does not touch the slowest stage should not be expected to make the design faster, and should not make another stage slower than it.
  • The block's internal delay is fixed. Soft logic between a block's output and the next register adds to that stage; blocks in series each add their delay plus a wire.
  • Moving or adding registers changes stage lengths and when values arrive.
  • Area falls when soft adders and flip-flops move into blocks.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone. Synthesis may already have placed the design's multiplies on tiles, so a block that only replaces one saves little: count tiles against the baseline.
Objective

Minimize area × delay × wirelength against the baseline. If you expect no rewrite to lower it, output TIER: NONE. Among rewrites that lower it, choose the one that lowers it most.

Output
Tiers
  • T1: The block replaces the region's arithmetic as it stands: the same operations on the same operands, now inside the block.
  • T2: The region's arithmetic is regrouped to fit the block (products regrouped into the block's sums, registers moved), computing the same values.
  • NONE: No rewrite: no candidate can be rewritten correctly.
Header

Write exactly this header, each key at the start of its own line, then the plan:

TIER: <exactly one of T1, T2, NONE>
REGIONS: <the converted candidate ids, comma-separated; NONE when TIER is NONE>
SHARED_REDUCTION: <the signal or module the converted products are summed in; NONE for a single region>
BLOCKS: <how many blocks the rewrite instantiates, one integer>
TILES: <how many DSP tiles the whole design then uses, one integer>
STAGE_NS: <the delay of the slowest stage the rewrite leaves, in ns, one number>
MAPPING: <which design signals go to which block ports>
PLAN: <the plan, stating everything listed below>

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output rules
  • Write nothing before the TIER line; read the source first.
  • A reviewer checks the plan automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.
  • If a change to the design itself, not to the rewrite, would let more of it use the block, you may say so on a line starting DESIGN_CHANGE:. It is reported to the user and does not change your decision.

Every filter is symmetric in the source (C6==C0, C5==C1, C4==C2 in each module's define block), so equal-coefficient taps are pre-added in soft logic at 17 bits and one 17-bit sum drives one 18-bit operand port; each block then carries two coefficient groups instead of one, which is what cuts the block count from 144 to 84 and the post-adder tree from two levels to one. Coefficients are taken from the module's own define through a 19-bit localparam (do not retype the numbers): localparam [18:0] C0 = COEF0_b;` and so on, one per coefficient the module uses.

    This is revision 1's rewrite with the block count per my_fir instance cut from two to one wherever the cheapest coefficient group can be done as a one-level shift-add in soft logic, off the critical path. 84 blocks become 48; the critical path keeps the same shape it has today.

Converted regions, by module (31 candidate ids, 6 instances each):

  • my_fir_f1, all 7 products (1486, 1487, 1488, 1489, 1490, 1491, 1492): the four coefficient groups 29/101/15/235 need two blocks. Doing two of them in soft would take three adder levels (29 = 32-2-1, then a combine), which lands at the final adder at about the same time as the block output (~6.3 ns vs 6.48 ns measured) and risks lengthening the only stage that matters. f1 therefore keeps 2 blocks per instance, 12 blocks over its 6 instances.
  • my_fir_f2, my_fir_h2, the C1/C5 and C2/C4 products (1543, 1544, 1546, 1547 and 1717, 1718, 1720, 1721): s1*42 + s2*163 is exactly one block. 1 block per instance, 12 blocks over 12 instances.
  • my_fir_f3, my_fir_h1, my_fir_h3, my_fir_h4, the C1/C5 and C2/C4 products (1603, 1604, 1605, 1606; 1662, 1663, 1664, 1665; 1776, 1777, 1778, 1779; 1834, 1835, 1836, 1837): s1*C1 + s2*C2 is exactly one block. 1 block per instance, 24 blocks over 24 instances.
    Total 48 blocks.

Candidates left, with reasons:

  • my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2, the C0/C6 and C3 products (1542, 1548, 1545 and 1716, 1722, 1719): C0 = 4 is a pure shift (s0*4 = {s0,2'b0}, no logic at all) and C3 = 255 = 256-1 is one subtract. Both are far cheaper in soft logic than the 253779-area tile a second block would cost, and they sit on a two-level soft path that reaches the final adder about 3 ns after the clock edge, well before the block output at ~6.5 ns, so they add nothing to the stage.
  • my_fir_f3, my_fir_h1, my_fir_h3, my_fir_h4, the C0/C6 products (1602, 1607; 1661, 1666; 1775, 1780; 1833, 1838): C0 is 12, 15, 9, 9 respectively, each a single shift-add on the 17-bit pre-add s0 (about 24 adder bits), again far cheaper than a second block and one level deep, so off the critical path.
  • All 46 fltr_compute_* candidates (fltr_compute_f1 7, f2 7, f3 6, h1 6, h2 7, h3 6, h4 7, each 6 instances): left. These are 8-bit by <=9-bit constant products that already pack several to a tile, 57 tiles for all 276 of them. Converting them needs 2 blocks per instance after symmetric pre-adding, 84 tiles, so +27 tiles (+6.9e6 area) against roughly 6400 soft bits saved (the six-level 20-bit adder trees and the q1..q7 registers, about 8.9e6): near a wash on area, but it raises the design's DSP count by a quarter, which is the thing that drove wirelength in this run (224 -> 143 tiles bought -23.8% wirelength), and it inserts a fresh register-to-block-to-register stage of about 1.42 + 1.07 + 1.17 + 2.14 + 2.25 = 8.05 ns where none exists today. On top of that, these sums sign-extend each 17-bit product ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q}) while the products are unsigned, so for coefficients 277 (f1), 364 (f3) and 324 (h4) the rewrite would have to recompute each product's bit 16 with a comparator and subtract 2^17 per set bit to stay bit-exact. Expected net: not an improvement, and inside the 9.4% seed noise even if it were.

Blocks and tiles: the rewrite instantiates 48 comb_sop_2_18 blocks (12 in my_fir_f1, 6 in each of the other six my_fir modules), each taking a DSP tile alone. The 59 tiles the design uses outside the my_fir multiplies (57 fltr_compute tiles plus 2) are untouched, so the design uses 107 DSP tiles, against 143 for the kept candidate and 224 for the baseline.

Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. No block feeds another; each block's result goes straight into one 28-bit soft add and then the dout register. The stage is register -> 17-bit pre-add (about 1.76 ns measured) -> wire into block (1.21) -> block (2.14) -> wire into the final add (1.27) -> 28-bit carry chain (0.53) -> the enable mux LUT the architecture needs for if (new_data_rdy) (1.65) -> flip-flop, about 8.6 ns, which is the slowest stage the rewrite leaves. That is the same shape and the same arithmetic depth as the 8.6427 ns measured for the kept candidate; one of its two block-to-adder inputs is replaced by a soft term that arrives roughly 3 ns earlier, and 36 fewer DSP tiles should, if anything, shorten the four long wires on that path. Against the 11.6069 ns baseline stage it is a 26% reduction.

Soft logic leaving and entering each stage: out of each my_fir dout stage (the baseline's slowest stage, 11.6069 ns in my_fir_f1 and 11.293 ns in my_fir_f2) go the six levels of 28-bit adders, about 168 adder bits per instance; what remains there is the three 17-bit pre-adds, one 28-bit final add, and for the eight instances-per-module groups listed above one extra shift-add term. Against the kept candidate, each of the 36 instances that drops a block gives back one 21-to-28-bit soft adder (f2/h2 give back two, one of which is a free shift), roughly 1.7e6 of soft area in exchange for 9.1e6 of tile area. No other stage is touched; the fltr_compute stages keep their multiplies and their adder trees exactly as they are, and they are below 8.6427 ns today since the measured period came from a my_fir path.

Register stages from operands to result, per converted region, before and after: unchanged at 0. In the baseline the products are combinational from din and n_delay_reg1..6 and the whole seven-term sum is captured by the dout register in the same cycle ("products registered 0 stages before the sum"); after the rewrite the pre-adds, the block, the soft shift-add terms and the final add are all combinational from the same registers and the result is captured by the same dout register in the same cycle, under the same new_data_rdy enable. No register is added, moved or removed, so no reset behaviour changes and nothing depends on a new register's initial value.

Correctness: each module's sum is regrouped only by the filter's own symmetry (C6==C0, C5==C1, C4==C2, checked against every `define group in the source: lines 1440-1449, 1500-1506, 1561-1567, 1616-1625, 1675-1681, 1734-1740, 1792-1798), and all operands and coefficients are unsigned, so the regrouping is exact. s0, s1, s2 are 17-bit and fit the 18-bit ax/bx ports zero-extended; coefficients are at most 255 and fit the 19-bit ay/by ports. Each block's true sum is at most 29.5e6 < 2^28, so the [27:0] slice of result loses nothing, and each module's full sum is at most 44.1e6 (f2/h2, 65535*673) < 2^28, so the 28-bit dout never wraps and matches the original bit for bit. The two subtractions used for constants ((d3<<8)-d3 and (s0<<4)-s0) can never borrow. No value computed inside a block is read anywhere else: q-style intermediates do not exist here, and n_delay_reg1..6 stay in soft registers because the delay line reads them.

DESIGN_CHANGE: in the seven fltr_compute_* modules the 17-bit products q1..q7 are unsigned (8-bit data times a positive constant) but the sum sign-extends them, {q[16],q[16],q[16],q}; dropping that sign extension (zero-extending instead) would make the fltr sums plain unsigned sums of products and let all 46 fltr candidates map onto the block without per-product bit-16 comparators and 2^17 corrections. It would change what the design computes for coefficients 277, 364 and 324, so it is not part of this rewrite.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Check
  • Every claim the plan makes about the design (who reads a value, a register's reset or enable, widths, cited lines, ASSUMES lines) against the source.
  • That the mapping as described keeps the same behavior.
  • That the plan states everything the planner's output section requires, listed below.

Do not judge cost or style; measurement decides cost.

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output
  • First line exactly APPROVE or REVISE.
  • If REVISE, for each problem: the rule it violates or the required item it omits, by name; the design lines; what to change.
  • Write nothing before the verdict line; read the source first. The verdict is applied automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.

MAPPING: Taps in every my_fir_* module are d0=din, d1..d6=n_delay_reg1..n_delay_reg6, all 16 bits unsigned. Every filter is symmetric in the source (C6==C0, C5==C1, C4==C2 in each module's define block), so equal-coefficient taps are pre-added in soft logic at 17 bits and one 17-bit sum drives one 18-bit operand port; each block then carries two coefficient groups instead of one, which is what cuts the block count from 144 to 84 and the post-adder tree from two levels to one. Coefficients are taken from the module's own define through a 19-bit localparam (do not retype the numbers): localparam [18:0] C0 = COEF0_b;` and so on, one per coefficient the module uses.

SHARED_REDUCTION: the dout sum of each my_fir_* module (one reduction per module instance: my_fir_f1.dout, my_fir_f2.dout, my_fir_f3.dout, my_fir_h1.dout, my_fir_h2.dout, my_fir_h3.dout, my_fir_h4.dout)
BLOCKS: 48
TILES: 107
STAGE_NS: 8.6
MAPPING: In every my_fir_* module the taps are d0=din, d1..d6=n_delay_reg1..n_delay_reg6, all 16-bit unsigned. Every filter is symmetric in the source (C6==C0, C5==C1, C4==C2 in each module's define group), so the three symmetric pairs are pre-added at 17 bits: wire[16:0] s0 = din + n_delay_reg6; wire[16:0] s1 = n_delay_reg1 + n_delay_reg5; wire[16:0] s2 = n_delay_reg2 + n_delay_reg4;. Coefficients that go to a block port are taken from the module's own define through a 19-bit localparam (do not retype the numbers): e.g. localparam[18:0] C1 = COEF1_c;`. Per module:

  • my_fir_f1 (_b, C0=29, C1=101, C2=15, C3=235) — two blocks, every port used:
    sop0 .ax({1'b0,s0}) .ay(C0) .bx({1'b0,s1}) .by(C1) .result(sop0_out);
    sop1 .ax({1'b0,s2}) .ay(C2) .bx({2'b0,n_delay_reg3}) .by(C3) .result(sop1_out);
    dout <= sop0_out[27:0] + sop1_out[27:0];
  • my_fir_f2 (_c) and my_fir_h2 (_2), C0=4, C1=42, C2=163, C3=255 — one block:
    sop0 .ax({1'b0,s1}) .ay(C1) .bx({1'b0,s2}) .by(C2) .result(sop0_out);
    soft: wire[27:0] t255 = {n_delay_reg3, 8'b0} - n_delay_reg3; (= d3*255, C3=255=256-1, never borrows) and wire[27:0] t_soft = t255 + {s0, 2'b0}; (the second term is s0*4, C0=4, a pure shift);
    dout <= sop0_out[27:0] + t_soft;
  • my_fir_f3 (_d, C0=12, C1=77, C2=148) — one block:
    sop0 .ax({1'b0,s1}) .ay(C1) .bx({1'b0,s2}) .by(C2);
    soft: wire[27:0] t_soft = {s0, 3'b0} + {s0, 2'b0}; (= s0*12);
    dout <= sop0_out[27:0] + t_soft;
  • my_fir_h1 (_1, C0=15, C1=25, C2=193) — one block:
    sop0 .ax({1'b0,s1}) .ay(C1) .bx({1'b0,s2}) .by(C2);
    soft: wire[27:0] t_soft = {s0, 4'b0} - s0; (= s0*15, never borrows);
    dout <= sop0_out[27:0] + t_soft;
  • my_fir_h3 (_3) and my_fir_h4 (_4), C0=9, C1=56, C2=109 — one block:
    sop0 .ax({1'b0,s1}) .ay(C1) .bx({1'b0,s2}) .by(C2);
    soft: wire[27:0] t_soft = {s0, 3'b0} + s0; (= s0*9);
    dout <= sop0_out[27:0] + t_soft;
    Every block instance uses all four input ports, so nothing is tied to 0. The always blocks keep their structure: only the dout <= right-hand side changes; n_delay_reg1..6 and output_data_ready are untouched.
    PLAN:
    This is revision 1's rewrite with the block count per my_fir instance cut from two to one wherever the cheapest coefficient group can be done as a one-level shift-add in soft logic, off the critical path. 84 blocks become 48; the critical path keeps the same shape it has today.

Converted regions, by module (31 candidate ids, 6 instances each):

  • my_fir_f1, all 7 products (1486, 1487, 1488, 1489, 1490, 1491, 1492): the four coefficient groups 29/101/15/235 need two blocks. Doing two of them in soft would take three adder levels (29 = 32-2-1, then a combine), which lands at the final adder at about the same time as the block output (~6.3 ns vs 6.48 ns measured) and risks lengthening the only stage that matters. f1 therefore keeps 2 blocks per instance, 12 blocks over its 6 instances.
  • my_fir_f2, my_fir_h2, the C1/C5 and C2/C4 products (1543, 1544, 1546, 1547 and 1717, 1718, 1720, 1721): s1*42 + s2*163 is exactly one block. 1 block per instance, 12 blocks over 12 instances.
  • my_fir_f3, my_fir_h1, my_fir_h3, my_fir_h4, the C1/C5 and C2/C4 products (1603, 1604, 1605, 1606; 1662, 1663, 1664, 1665; 1776, 1777, 1778, 1779; 1834, 1835, 1836, 1837): s1*C1 + s2*C2 is exactly one block. 1 block per instance, 24 blocks over 24 instances.
    Total 48 blocks.

Candidates left, with reasons:

  • my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2, the C0/C6 and C3 products (1542, 1548, 1545 and 1716, 1722, 1719): C0 = 4 is a pure shift (s0*4 = {s0,2'b0}, no logic at all) and C3 = 255 = 256-1 is one subtract. Both are far cheaper in soft logic than the 253779-area tile a second block would cost, and they sit on a two-level soft path that reaches the final adder about 3 ns after the clock edge, well before the block output at ~6.5 ns, so they add nothing to the stage.
  • my_fir_f3, my_fir_h1, my_fir_h3, my_fir_h4, the C0/C6 products (1602, 1607; 1661, 1666; 1775, 1780; 1833, 1838): C0 is 12, 15, 9, 9 respectively, each a single shift-add on the 17-bit pre-add s0 (about 24 adder bits), again far cheaper than a second block and one level deep, so off the critical path.
  • All 46 fltr_compute_* candidates (fltr_compute_f1 7, f2 7, f3 6, h1 6, h2 7, h3 6, h4 7, each 6 instances): left. These are 8-bit by <=9-bit constant products that already pack several to a tile, 57 tiles for all 276 of them. Converting them needs 2 blocks per instance after symmetric pre-adding, 84 tiles, so +27 tiles (+6.9e6 area) against roughly 6400 soft bits saved (the six-level 20-bit adder trees and the q1..q7 registers, about 8.9e6): near a wash on area, but it raises the design's DSP count by a quarter, which is the thing that drove wirelength in this run (224 -> 143 tiles bought -23.8% wirelength), and it inserts a fresh register-to-block-to-register stage of about 1.42 + 1.07 + 1.17 + 2.14 + 2.25 = 8.05 ns where none exists today. On top of that, these sums sign-extend each 17-bit product ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q}) while the products are unsigned, so for coefficients 277 (f1), 364 (f3) and 324 (h4) the rewrite would have to recompute each product's bit 16 with a comparator and subtract 2^17 per set bit to stay bit-exact. Expected net: not an improvement, and inside the 9.4% seed noise even if it were.

Blocks and tiles: the rewrite instantiates 48 comb_sop_2_18 blocks (12 in my_fir_f1, 6 in each of the other six my_fir modules), each taking a DSP tile alone. The 59 tiles the design uses outside the my_fir multiplies (57 fltr_compute tiles plus 2) are untouched, so the design uses 107 DSP tiles, against 143 for the kept candidate and 224 for the baseline.

Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. No block feeds another; each block's result goes straight into one 28-bit soft add and then the dout register. The stage is register -> 17-bit pre-add (about 1.76 ns measured) -> wire into block (1.21) -> block (2.14) -> wire into the final add (1.27) -> 28-bit carry chain (0.53) -> the enable mux LUT the architecture needs for if (new_data_rdy) (1.65) -> flip-flop, about 8.6 ns, which is the slowest stage the rewrite leaves. That is the same shape and the same arithmetic depth as the 8.6427 ns measured for the kept candidate; one of its two block-to-adder inputs is replaced by a soft term that arrives roughly 3 ns earlier, and 36 fewer DSP tiles should, if anything, shorten the four long wires on that path. Against the 11.6069 ns baseline stage it is a 26% reduction.

Soft logic leaving and entering each stage: out of each my_fir dout stage (the baseline's slowest stage, 11.6069 ns in my_fir_f1 and 11.293 ns in my_fir_f2) go the six levels of 28-bit adders, about 168 adder bits per instance; what remains there is the three 17-bit pre-adds, one 28-bit final add, and for the eight instances-per-module groups listed above one extra shift-add term. Against the kept candidate, each of the 36 instances that drops a block gives back one 21-to-28-bit soft adder (f2/h2 give back two, one of which is a free shift), roughly 1.7e6 of soft area in exchange for 9.1e6 of tile area. No other stage is touched; the fltr_compute stages keep their multiplies and their adder trees exactly as they are, and they are below 8.6427 ns today since the measured period came from a my_fir path.

Register stages from operands to result, per converted region, before and after: unchanged at 0. In the baseline the products are combinational from din and n_delay_reg1..6 and the whole seven-term sum is captured by the dout register in the same cycle ("products registered 0 stages before the sum"); after the rewrite the pre-adds, the block, the soft shift-add terms and the final add are all combinational from the same registers and the result is captured by the same dout register in the same cycle, under the same new_data_rdy enable. No register is added, moved or removed, so no reset behaviour changes and nothing depends on a new register's initial value.

Correctness: each module's sum is regrouped only by the filter's own symmetry (C6==C0, C5==C1, C4==C2, checked against every `define group in the source: lines 1440-1449, 1500-1506, 1561-1567, 1616-1625, 1675-1681, 1734-1740, 1792-1798), and all operands and coefficients are unsigned, so the regrouping is exact. s0, s1, s2 are 17-bit and fit the 18-bit ax/bx ports zero-extended; coefficients are at most 255 and fit the 19-bit ay/by ports. Each block's true sum is at most 29.5e6 < 2^28, so the [27:0] slice of result loses nothing, and each module's full sum is at most 44.1e6 (f2/h2, 65535*673) < 2^28, so the 28-bit dout never wraps and matches the original bit for bit. The two subtractions used for constants ((d3<<8)-d3 and (s0<<4)-s0) can never borrow. No value computed inside a block is read anywhere else: q-style intermediates do not exist here, and n_delay_reg1..6 stay in soft registers because the delay line reads them.

DESIGN_CHANGE: in the seven fltr_compute_* modules the 17-bit products q1..q7 are unsigned (8-bit data times a positive constant) but the sum sign-extends them, {q[16],q[16],q[16],q}; dropping that sign extension (zero-extending instead) would make the fltr sums plain unsigned sums of products and let all 46 fltr candidates map onto the block without per-product bit-16 comparators and 2^17 corrections. It would change what the design computes for coefficients 277, 364 and 324, so it is not part of this rewrite.

Reference simulation

After the edit, the framework simulates the edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle. A candidate that does not match is not measured. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (comb_sop_2_18.v) are in sim_reference/.

Both are far cheaper in soft logic than the 253779-area tile a second block would cost, and they sit on a two-level soft path that reaches the final adder about 3 ns after the clock edge, well before the block output at ~6.5 ns, so they add nothing to the stage.

These are 8-bit by <=9-bit constant products that already pack several to a tile, 57 tiles for all 276 of them. Converting them needs 2 blocks per instance after symmetric pre-adding, 84 tiles, so +27 tiles (+6.9e6 area) against roughly 6400 soft bits saved (the six-level 20-bit adder trees and the q1..q7 registers, about 8.9e6): near a wash on area, but it raises the design's DSP count by a quarter, which is the thing that drove wirelength in this run (224 -> 143 tiles bought -23.8% wirelength), and it inserts a fresh register-to-block-to-register stage of about 1.42 + 1.07 + 1.17 + 2.14 + 2.25 = 8.05 ns where none exists today. On top of that, these sums sign-extend each 17-bit product ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q}) while the products are unsigned, so for coefficients 277 (f1), 364 (f3) and 324 (h4) the rewrite would have to recompute each product's bit 16 with a comparator and subtract 2^17 per set bit to stay bit-exact. Expected net: not an improvement, and inside the 9.4% seed noise even if it were.

Blocks and tiles: the rewrite instantiates 48 comb_sop_2_18 blocks (12 in my_fir_f1, 6 in each of the other six my_fir modules), each taking a DSP tile alone. The 59 tiles the design uses outside the my_fir multiplies (57 fltr_compute tiles plus 2) are untouched, so the design uses 107 DSP tiles, against 143 for the kept candidate and 224 for the baseline.

Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. No block feeds another; each block's result goes straight into one 28-bit soft add and then the dout register. The stage is register -> 17-bit pre-add (about 1.76 ns measured) -> wire into block (1.21) -> block (2.14) -> wire into the final add (1.27) -> 28-bit carry chain (0.53) -> the enable mux LUT the architecture needs for if (new_data_rdy) (1.65) -> flip-flop, about 8.6 ns, which is the slowest stage the rewrite leaves. That is the same shape and the same arithmetic depth as the 8.6427 ns measured for the kept candidate; one of its two block-to-adder inputs is replaced by a soft term that arrives roughly 3 ns earlier, and 36 fewer DSP tiles should, if anything, shorten the four long wires on that path. Against the 11.6069 ns baseline stage it is a 26% reduction.

Soft logic leaving and entering each stage: out of each my_fir dout stage (the baseline's slowest stage, 11.6069 ns in my_fir_f1 and 11.293 ns in my_fir_f2) go the six levels of 28-bit adders, about 168 adder bits per instance; what remains there is the three 17-bit pre-adds, one 28-bit final add, and for the eight instances-per-module groups listed above one extra shift-add term. Against the kept candidate, each of the 36 instances that drops a block gives back one 21-to-28-bit soft adder (f2/h2 give back two, one of which is a free shift), roughly 1.7e6 of soft area in exchange for 9.1e6 of tile area. No other stage is touched; the fltr_compute stages keep their multiplies and their adder trees exactly as they are, and they are below 8.6427 ns today since the measured period came from a my_fir path.

Register stages from operands to result, per converted region, before and after: unchanged at 0. In the baseline the products are combinational from din and n_delay_reg1..6 and the whole seven-term sum is captured by the dout register in the same cycle ("products registered 0 stages before the sum"); after the rewrite the pre-adds, the block, the soft shift-add terms and the final add are all combinational from the same registers and the result is captured by the same dout register in the same cycle, under the same new_data_rdy enable. No register is added, moved or removed, so no reset behaviour changes and nothing depends on a new register's initial value.

Correctness: each module's sum is regrouped only by the filter's own symmetry (C6==C0, C5==C1, C4==C2, checked against every `define group in the source: lines 1440-1449, 1500-1506, 1561-1567, 1616-1625, 1675-1681, 1734-1740, 1792-1798), and all operands and coefficients are unsigned, so the regrouping is exact. s0, s1, s2 are 17-bit and fit the 18-bit ax/bx ports zero-extended; coefficients are at most 255 and fit the 19-bit ay/by ports. Each block's true sum is at most 29.5e6 < 2^28, so the [27:0] slice of result loses nothing, and each module's full sum is at most 44.1e6 (f2/h2, 65535*673) < 2^28, so the 28-bit dout never wraps and matches the original bit for bit. The two subtractions used for constants ((d3<<8)-d3 and (s0<<4)-s0) can never borrow. No value computed inside a block is read anywhere else: q-style intermediates do not exist here, and n_delay_reg1..6 stay in soft registers because the delay line reads them.

Simulation

When you finish, the framework simulates your edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle, on its own copy. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (comb_sop_2_18.v) are in sim_reference/; you may read them, but editing them has no effect on the result.

What changed, region by region

Common to all seven my_fir_* modules: the three symmetric tap pairs are pre-added at 17 bits (s0 = din + n_delay_reg6, s1 = n_delay_reg1 + n_delay_reg5, s2 = n_delay_reg2 + n_delay_reg4), valid because each filter's define group has C6==C0, C5==C1, C4==C2. Coefficients reaching a block port are taken from the module's own define through a 19-bit localparam. The always blocks keep their structure — only the dout <= right-hand side changed; n_delay_reg1..6 and output_data_ready are untouched, so no register is added, moved, or reset differently.

  • my_fir_f1 — regions 1486, 1487, 1488, 1489, 1490, 1491, 1492 (all 7 products): two blocks, every port used. sop0 = s0*C0 + s1*C1 (29, 101); sop1 = s2*C2 + n_delay_reg3*C3 (15, 235). dout <= sop0_out[27:0] + sop1_out[27:0].
  • my_fir_f2 — regions 1543, 1544, 1546, 1547: one block, s1*42 + s2*163. The C3 and C0 terms stay in soft logic as t255 = {n_delay_reg3,8'b0} - n_delay_reg3 (×255) and t_soft = t255 + {s0,2'b0} (+ s0×4). dout <= sop0_out[27:0] + t_soft.
  • my_fir_f3 — regions 1603, 1604, 1605, 1606: one block, s1*77 + s2*148; soft t_soft = {s0,3'b0} + {s0,2'b0} (= s0×12).
  • my_fir_h1 — regions 1662, 1663, 1664, 1665: one block, s1*25 + s2*193; soft t_soft = {s0,4'b0} - s0 (= s0×15).
  • my_fir_h2 — regions 1717, 1718, 1720, 1721: identical to my_fir_f2 (same coefficient group 4/42/163/255).
  • my_fir_h3 — regions 1776, 1777, 1778, 1779: one block, s1*56 + s2*109; soft t_soft = {s0,3'b0} + s0 (= s0×9).
  • my_fir_h4 — regions 1834, 1835, 1836, 1837: identical to my_fir_h3 (same group 9/56/109).

Every block instance drives all four input ports, so nothing is tied to 0. Each block's internal sum stays below 2^28 (largest is f1's s2*15 + d3*235 ≈ 17.4 M) so the [27:0] slice of result is lossless, and each module's full sum peaks at 65535×673 ≈ 44.1 M < 2^28, so the 28-bit final add never wraps. The two constant subtractions, (d3<<8)-d3 and (s0<<4)-s0, cannot borrow. No value computed inside a block is read anywhere else; the delay registers stay in soft logic because the delay line reads them. No assumptions about the design's inputs are needed.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Inner-loop check: the front end of the real flow, then a cell census. NOT place-and-route.
# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
# Reads, in the flow's order: blocks.vlib (every hard block of the architecture, declared from its
# models), primitives.vlib (the flow's library of memories, adders and multipliers), then the design;
# then elaborates with the flow's hierarchy check. A module that is not defined, a port name the
# block does not have, or a misspelled block name fails here as it would in the flow. Do not
# declare the target block in the design: blocks.vlib declares it, and a design that defines a module
# of the target block's name fails this check.
# Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole design (the last "Number of cells"
# table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub, registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as
# $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated module by name, which is where a hard-block
# instantiation shows up with its instance count.
set -u
f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
lib=""
[ -f "$here/blocks.vlib" ] && lib="read_verilog -lib $here/blocks.vlib; "
[ -f "$here/primitives.vlib" ] && lib="${lib}read_verilog -nomem2reg $here/primitives.vlib; "
target="$(sed -n 's|^// target block: *\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*\).*|\1|p' "$here/blocks.vlib" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
if [ -n "$target" ] && grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*module[[:space:]]+$target([^A-Za-z0-9_$]|$)" "$f"; then
  echo "FAIL: $f defines module $target; blocks.vlib declares it. Remove the module definition and keep the instances."
  exit 1
fi
out="$(yosys -p "${lib}read_verilog -sv -nolatches $f; hierarchy -check -auto-top -purge_lib; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
  echo "$out" | tail -10
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
                   on {on=0}
                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true
// comb_sop_2_18: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx*by, all four operands unsigned
// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); each 18x19 product is 37
// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
// Ports: ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every
// input reaches result in the same cycle.
module comb_sop_2_18 (
    input  [17:0] ax,
    input  [18:0] ay,
    input  [17:0] bx,
    input  [18:0] by,
    output [63:0] result
);

    wire [36:0] prod_a = ax * ay;                                    // 18x19 -> 37, exact
    wire [36:0] prod_b = bx * by;                                    // 18x19 -> 37, exact
    wire [63:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b;                            // zero-extended, exact

    assign result = sum;

endmodule

    input clk;

    output[28 - 1:0] dout;

	input new_data_rdy;
	output output_data_ready;
	reg output_data_ready;

    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg1;

    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg3;

    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg5;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg6;

    always @(posedge clk)

		if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1)

			n_delay_reg1 <= din;
			n_delay_reg2 <= n_delay_reg1;
			n_delay_reg3 <= n_delay_reg2;
			n_delay_reg4 <= n_delay_reg3;
			n_delay_reg5 <= n_delay_reg4;
			n_delay_reg6 <= n_delay_reg5;
		
			output_data_ready <= 1'b1;
			dout <= (din * `COEF0_b) + 
				(n_delay_reg1 * `COEF1_b) + 
				(n_delay_reg2 * `COEF2_b) + 
				(n_delay_reg3 * `COEF3_b) + 
				(n_delay_reg4 * `COEF4_b) + 
				(n_delay_reg5 * `COEF5_b) + 
				(n_delay_reg6 * `COEF6_b);
		end
		else
		begin
			output_data_ready <= 1'b0;
		end
	end
endmodule

  • my_fir_f1 (_b, C0=29, C1=101, C2=15, C3=235) — two blocks, every port used:
    sop0 .ax({1'b0,s0}) .ay(C0) .bx({1'b0,s1}) .by(C1) .result(sop0_out);
    sop1 .ax({1'b0,s2}) .ay(C2) .bx({2'b0,n_delay_reg3}) .by(C3) .result(sop1_out);
    dout <= sop0_out[27:0] + sop1_out[27:0];
  • my_fir_f2 (_c) and my_fir_h2 (_2), C0=4, C1=42, C2=163, C3=255 — one block:
    sop0 .ax({1'b0,s1}) .ay(C1) .bx({1'b0,s2}) .by(C2) .result(sop0_out);
    soft: wire[27:0] t255 = {n_delay_reg3, 8'b0} - n_delay_reg3; (= d3*255, C3=255=256-1, never borrows) and wire[27:0] t_soft = t255 + {s0, 2'b0}; (the second term is s0*4, C0=4, a pure shift);
    dout <= sop0_out[27:0] + t_soft;
  • my_fir_f3 (_d, C0=12, C1=77, C2=148) — one block:
    sop0 .ax({1'b0,s1}) .ay(C1) .bx({1'b0,s2}) .by(C2);
    soft: wire[27:0] t_soft = {s0, 3'b0} + {s0, 2'b0}; (= s0*12);
    dout <= sop0_out[27:0] + t_soft;
  • my_fir_h1 (_1, C0=15, C1=25, C2=193) — one block:
    sop0 .ax({1'b0,s1}) .ay(C1) .bx({1'b0,s2}) .by(C2);
    soft: wire[27:0] t_soft = {s0, 4'b0} - s0; (= s0*15, never borrows);
    dout <= sop0_out[27:0] + t_soft;
  • my_fir_h3 (_3) and my_fir_h4 (_4), C0=9, C1=56, C2=109 — one block:
    sop0 .ax({1'b0,s1}) .ay(C1) .bx({1'b0,s2}) .by(C2);
    soft: wire[27:0] t_soft = {s0, 3'b0} + s0; (= s0*9);
    dout <= sop0_out[27:0] + t_soft;
    Every block instance uses all four input ports, so nothing is tied to 0. The always blocks keep their structure: only the dout <= right-hand side changes; n_delay_reg1..6 and output_data_ready are untouched.
    PLAN:
    This is revision 1's rewrite with the block count per my_fir instance cut from two to one wherever the cheapest coefficient group can be done as a one-level shift-add in soft logic, off the critical path. 84 blocks become 48; the critical path keeps the same shape it has today.

Converted regions, by module (31 candidate ids, 6 instances each):

  • my_fir_f1, all 7 products (1486, 1487, 1488, 1489, 1490, 1491, 1492): the four coefficient groups 29/101/15/235 need two blocks. Doing two of them in soft would take three adder levels (29 = 32-2-1, then a combine), which lands at the final adder at about the same time as the block output (~6.3 ns vs 6.48 ns measured) and risks lengthening the only stage that matters. f1 therefore keeps 2 blocks per instance, 12 blocks over its 6 instances.
  • my_fir_f2, my_fir_h2, the C1/C5 and C2/C4 products (1543, 1544, 1546, 1547 and 1717, 1718, 1720, 1721): s1*42 + s2*163 is exactly one block. 1 block per instance, 12 blocks over 12 instances.
  • my_fir_f3, my_fir_h1, my_fir_h3, my_fir_h4, the C1/C5 and C2/C4 products (1603, 1604, 1605, 1606; 1662, 1663, 1664, 1665; 1776, 1777, 1778, 1779; 1834, 1835, 1836, 1837): s1*C1 + s2*C2 is exactly one block. 1 block per instance, 24 blocks over 24 instances.
    Total 48 blocks.

Candidates left, with reasons:

  • my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2, the C0/C6 and C3 products (1542, 1548, 1545 and 1716, 1722, 1719): C0 = 4 is a pure shift (s0*4 = {s0,2'b0}, no logic at all) and C3 = 255 = 256-1 is one subtract. Both are far cheaper in soft logic than the 253779-area tile a second block would cost, and they sit on a two-level soft path that reaches the final adder about 3 ns after the clock edge, well before the block output at ~6.5 ns, so they add nothing to the stage.
  • my_fir_f3, my_fir_h1, my_fir_h3, my_fir_h4, the C0/C6 products (1602, 1607; 1661, 1666; 1775, 1780; 1833, 1838): C0 is 12, 15, 9, 9 respectively, each a single shift-add on the 17-bit pre-add s0 (about 24 adder bits), again far cheaper than a second block and one level deep, so off the critical path.
  • All 46 fltr_compute_* candidates (fltr_compute_f1 7, f2 7, f3 6, h1 6, h2 7, h3 6, h4 7, each 6 instances): left. These are 8-bit by <=9-bit constant products that already pack several to a tile, 57 tiles for all 276 of them. Converting them needs 2 blocks per instance after symmetric pre-adding, 84 tiles, so +27 tiles (+6.9e6 area) against roughly 6400 soft bits saved (the six-level 20-bit adder trees and the q1..q7 registers, about 8.9e6): near a wash on area, but it raises the design's DSP count by a quarter, which is the thing that drove wirelength in this run (224 -> 143 tiles bought -23.8% wirelength), and it inserts a fresh register-to-block-to-register stage of about 1.42 + 1.07 + 1.17 + 2.14 + 2.25 = 8.05 ns where none exists today. On top of that, these sums sign-extend each 17-bit product ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q}) while the products are unsigned, so for coefficients 277 (f1), 364 (f3) and 324 (h4) the rewrite would have to recompute each product's bit 16 with a comparator and subtract 2^17 per set bit to stay bit-exact. Expected net: not an improvement, and inside the 9.4% seed noise even if it were.

Blocks and tiles: the rewrite instantiates 48 comb_sop_2_18 blocks (12 in my_fir_f1, 6 in each of the other six my_fir modules), each taking a DSP tile alone. The 59 tiles the design uses outside the my_fir multiplies (57 fltr_compute tiles plus 2) are untouched, so the design uses 107 DSP tiles, against 143 for the kept candidate and 224 for the baseline.

Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. No block feeds another; each block's result goes straight into one 28-bit soft add and then the dout register. The stage is register -> 17-bit pre-add (about 1.76 ns measured) -> wire into block (1.21) -> block (2.14) -> wire into the final add (1.27) -> 28-bit carry chain (0.53) -> the enable mux LUT the architecture needs for if (new_data_rdy) (1.65) -> flip-flop, about 8.6 ns, which is the slowest stage the rewrite leaves. That is the same shape and the same arithmetic depth as the 8.6427 ns measured for the kept candidate; one of its two block-to-adder inputs is replaced by a soft term that arrives roughly 3 ns earlier, and 36 fewer DSP tiles should, if anything, shorten the four long wires on that path. Against the 11.6069 ns baseline stage it is a 26% reduction.

Soft logic leaving and entering each stage: out of each my_fir dout stage (the baseline's slowest stage, 11.6069 ns in my_fir_f1 and 11.293 ns in my_fir_f2) go the six levels of 28-bit adders, about 168 adder bits per instance; what remains there is the three 17-bit pre-adds, one 28-bit final add, and for the eight instances-per-module groups listed above one extra shift-add term. Against the kept candidate, each of the 36 instances that drops a block gives back one 21-to-28-bit soft adder (f2/h2 give back two, one of which is a free shift), roughly 1.7e6 of soft area in exchange for 9.1e6 of tile area. No other stage is touched; the fltr_compute stages keep their multiplies and their adder trees exactly as they are, and they are below 8.6427 ns today since the measured period came from a my_fir path.

Register stages from operands to result, per converted region, before and after: unchanged at 0. In the baseline the products are combinational from din and n_delay_reg1..6 and the whole seven-term sum is captured by the dout register in the same cycle ("products registered 0 stages before the sum"); after the rewrite the pre-adds, the block, the soft shift-add terms and the final add are all combinational from the same registers and the result is captured by the same dout register in the same cycle, under the same new_data_rdy enable. No register is added, moved or removed, so no reset behaviour changes and nothing depends on a new register's initial value.

Correctness: each module's sum is regrouped only by the filter's own symmetry (C6==C0, C5==C1, C4==C2, checked against every `define group in the source: lines 1440-1449, 1500-1506, 1561-1567, 1616-1625, 1675-1681, 1734-1740, 1792-1798), and all operands and coefficients are unsigned, so the regrouping is exact. s0, s1, s2 are 17-bit and fit the 18-bit ax/bx ports zero-extended; coefficients are at most 255 and fit the 19-bit ay/by ports. Each block's true sum is at most 29.5e6 < 2^28, so the [27:0] slice of result loses nothing, and each module's full sum is at most 44.1e6 (f2/h2, 65535*673) < 2^28, so the 28-bit dout never wraps and matches the original bit for bit. The two subtractions used for constants ((d3<<8)-d3 and (s0<<4)-s0) can never borrow. No value computed inside a block is read anywhere else: q-style intermediates do not exist here, and n_delay_reg1..6 stay in soft registers because the delay line reads them.

DESIGN_CHANGE: in the seven fltr_compute_* modules the 17-bit products q1..q7 are unsigned (8-bit data times a positive constant) but the sum sign-extends them, {q[16],q[16],q[16],q}; dropping that sign extension (zero-extending instead) would make the fltr sums plain unsigned sums of products and let all 46 fltr candidates map onto the block without per-product bit-16 comparators and 2^17 corrections. It would change what the design computes for coefficients 277, 364 and 324, so it is not part of this rewrite.

Eight comb_sop_2_18 instances exist in the file (1487, 1488, 1550, 1620, 1689, 1754, 1823, 1891): two in my_fir_f1, one in each of the other six — exactly the 48-blocks-over-6-copies split the plan names. The fltr_compute_* sign-extended sums at 867-1073 are untouched, so the declared DESIGN_CHANGE was correctly not applied. Only other change is trailing-whitespace removal on the lines adjacent to the edited dout assignments.

Port connection. Every instance connects all four input ports by name; no port is left floating and none is tied to 0 (consistent with the plan, which claims all four used everywhere). ax/bx get 18 bits ({1'b0,s0/s1/s2} = 18, {2'b0,n_delay_reg3} = 18); ay/by get the 19-bit localparams taken from the module's own define. result drives only the local sop*_out wires, which feed only the dout` right-hand side.

Arithmetic. WIDTH_5B = 16 (1451), so taps are 16-bit unsigned; s0/s1/s2 at 17 bits hold the pre-add carry exactly. Symmetry holds in every define group (1440-1449, 1510-1516, 1581-1587, 1646-1655, 1715-1721, 1784-1790, 1852-1858): C6==C0, C5==C1, C4==C2, and COEF3 is 0 in f3/h1/h3/h4, which matches the original expressions that omit the d3 term. The soft terms are exact: {d3,8'b0}-d3 = 255·d3 and {s0,4'b0}-s0 = 15·s0 in 28-bit unsigned context, neither can borrow; {s0,3'b0}+{s0,2'b0} = 12·s0, {s0,3'b0}+s0 = 9·s0, {s0,2'b0} = 4·s0. Each block's true sum is at most 29.5e6 and each module's total at most 65535·673 = 44.1e6, both under 2^28, so the [27:0] slices and the 28-bit dout` lose nothing; the original 32-bit-context sum also fits, so the two agree bit for bit.

Visibility / registers / reset. No value computed inside a block is read elsewhere — the original had no named product intermediates, and n_delay_reg1..6 stay in soft registers feeding the delay line. No register is added, moved, or removed; the delay chain, output_data_ready, and the new_data_rdy enable are unchanged, so reset behaviour is identical and nothing depends on a new register's initial value. No ASSUMES line is needed, and none is claimed.

1	// comb_sop_2_18: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx*by, all four operands unsigned
2	// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); each 18x19 product is 37
3	// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
4	// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
5	// Ports: ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every
6	// input reaches result in the same cycle.
7	module comb_sop_2_18 (
8	    input  [17:0] ax,
9	    input  [18:0] ay,
10	    input  [17:0] bx,
11	    input  [18:0] by,
12	    output [63:0] result
13	);
14	
15	    wire [36:0] prod_a = ax * ay;                                    // 18x19 -> 37, exact
16	    wire [36:0] prod_b = bx * by;                                    // 18x19 -> 37, exact
17	    wire [63:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b;                            // zero-extended, exact
18	
19	    assign result = sum;
20	
21	endmodule

Task

You are the planner. Read the design source, stereovision2.v, and decide which of the candidate arithmetic regions listed below to rewrite onto the hard block described next, or that none should be rewritten. Write a plan for the editor, who carries it out; do not edit any file.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: comb_sop_2_18 (precision INT19)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx*by
  • input ports: ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19]
  • output ports: result[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and result is valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0.
The design

Baseline: the unmodified stereovision2 under this run's VPR settings (channel width 300, median of five seeds, 1 to 5) has a worst register-to-register path of 11.6069 ns on its one clock tm3_clk_v0 (I/O pads not timed) and uses 224 DSP tiles (as packed at seed 1) of the device's 306. Its used logic-block area is 9.73358e+07 minimum-width transistor areas (one DSP tile 253779, one cluster 27905) and its routed wirelength is 436921, so its area x delay x wirelength product, the objective, is 4.93619e+14. Its slowest stage (read off the seed-1 timing report) is in my_fir_f1: one hard multiply on a DSP tile (two_mult_18x19), then six adder levels with their carry chains, then one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop. Any path your rewrite creates is compared against that critical path.
