Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Cost (guidance: go against it only with a reason in the plan)
  • The clock period is the delay of the slowest stage (the logic between one register and the next). A rewrite that does not touch the slowest stage should not be expected to make the design faster, and should not make another stage slower than it.
  • The block's internal delay is fixed. Soft logic between a block's output and the next register adds to that stage; blocks in series each add their delay plus a wire.
  • Moving or adding registers changes stage lengths and when values arrive.
  • Area falls when soft adders and flip-flops move into blocks.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone. Synthesis may already have placed the design's multiplies on tiles, so a block that only replaces one saves little: count tiles against the baseline.
Objective

Minimize area × delay × wirelength against the baseline. If you expect no rewrite to lower it, output TIER: NONE. Among rewrites that lower it, choose the one that lowers it most.

Output
Tiers
  • T1: The block replaces the region's arithmetic as it stands: the same operations on the same operands, now inside the block.
  • T2: The region's arithmetic is regrouped to fit the block (products regrouped into the block's sums, registers moved), computing the same values.
  • NONE: No rewrite: no candidate can be rewritten correctly.
Header

Write exactly this header, each key at the start of its own line, then the plan:

TIER: <exactly one of T1, T2, NONE>
REGIONS: <the converted candidate ids, comma-separated; NONE when TIER is NONE>
SHARED_REDUCTION: <the signal or module the converted products are summed in; NONE for a single region>
BLOCKS: <how many blocks the rewrite instantiates, one integer>
TILES: <how many DSP tiles the whole design then uses, one integer>
STAGE_NS: <the delay of the slowest stage the rewrite leaves, in ns, one number>
MAPPING: <which design signals go to which block ports>
PLAN: <the plan, stating everything listed below>

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output rules
  • Write nothing before the TIER line; read the source first.
  • A reviewer checks the plan automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.
  • If a change to the design itself, not to the rewrite, would let more of it use the block, you may say so on a line starting DESIGN_CHANGE:. It is reported to the user and does not change your decision.

The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (comb_sop_2_18.v) are in sim_reference/.

PLAN:

What this plan is

It keeps the kept candidate's my_fir rewrite exactly as measured (48 blocks, period 8.202 ns at seed 1) and adds the same treatment to the seven fltr_compute_* modules, which the kept candidate left entirely alone. The fltr side is where the remaining soft arithmetic of this design sits: 42 instances (7 modules x 6), each a seven-tap symmetric FIR whose 7 registered products are summed by a six-level chain of 20-bit adders. That chain disappears; the 57-59 mult_9x9 tiles that hold the fltr products are replaced by 48 blocks. The period is set by the my_fir stage and is untouched; the gain is area and wirelength.

Apply both parts to the unmodified stereovision2.v in this directory.

Part A - my_fir_* (reproduce the kept candidate verbatim)

In every my_fir_* module insert, before the always block:

verilog
	// symmetric taps pre-added: COEF6==COEF0, COEF5==COEF1, COEF4==COEF2
	wire[16:0] s0 = din + n_delay_reg6;
	wire[16:0] s1 = n_delay_reg1 + n_delay_reg5;
	wire[16:0] s2 = n_delay_reg2 + n_delay_reg4;

and the localparams/blocks/soft terms below; replace only the dout <= ... sum inside if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1), leaving the delay-line shifts, output_data_ready and the else branch alone.

  • my_fir_f1 (_b, 29,101,15,235,15,101,29): localparam[18:0] C0=COEF0_b, C1=COEF1_b, C2=COEF2_b, C3=COEF3_b; two blocks, sop0(.ax({1'b0,s0}),.ay(C0),.bx({1'b0,s1}),.by(C1),.result(sop0_out)), sop1(.ax({1'b0,s2}),.ay(C2),.bx({2'b0,n_delay_reg3}),.by(C3),.result(sop1_out)), and dout <= sop0_out[27:0] + sop1_out[27:0];
  • my_fir_f2 (_c) and my_fir_h2 (_2): one block on C1,C2 as in MAPPING; wire[27:0] t255 = {n_delay_reg3, 8'b0} - n_delay_reg3; wire[27:0] t_soft = t255 + {s0, 2'b0}; dout <= sop0_out[27:0] + t_soft; (COEF3==255 and COEF0==4 stay soft shifts)
  • my_fir_f3 (_d): one block on C1,C2; wire[27:0] t_soft = {s0, 3'b0} + {s0, 2'b0}; (COEF0==12)
  • my_fir_h1 (_1): one block on C1,C2; wire[27:0] t_soft = {s0, 4'b0} - s0; (COEF0==15)
  • my_fir_h3 (_3) and my_fir_h4 (_4): one block on C1,C2; wire[27:0] t_soft = {s0, 3'b0} + s0; (COEF0==9)

All seven coefficient sets of my_fir are below 258 and all sums fit the 28-bit dout (largest 673*65535 = 4.4e7 < 2^28), so the regrouping is bit-exact; this part is already confirmed by the reference simulation of the kept candidate.

Part B - fltr_compute_* (new)

Each fltr_compute_* module is

q_i <= d_i * C_i                                  (stage 1)
d_out_tmp <= sum of sign_extend20(q_i)            (stage 2, six adder levels)
dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3]                           (stage 3, wires only)

with C7==C1, C6==C2, C5==C3 in all seven modules, so the 7 products are 4 distinct products of the pre-sums s1=d1+d7, s2=d2+d6, s3=d3+d5 and the centre tap d4.

Two facts make the regrouping exact:

  1. Each q_i is 17 bits and no product of this design overflows 17 bits (largest is 255*364 = 92820), and the true sum S = sum_i(d_i*C_i) never reaches 2^20 (largest module total 510*563 = 287130 for f3), so S may be formed at 20 bits with no wrap, and the pair products (d1+d7)*C1 etc. are exact.
  2. The source sign-extends each unsigned q_i by replicating q_i[16] into bits 19:17, which is worth -2^17*q_i[16] modulo 2^20. So the register the source writes is d_out_tmp = S - 2^17*B (mod 2^20), with B = sum_i q_i[16]. q_i[16] can only be 1 when 255*C_i >= 65536, i.e. C_i >= 258; that happens for exactly three coefficients in the whole design: f1's C4=277 (set iff d4 >= 237), f3's C3=C5=364 (set iff d3 >= 181, resp. d5 >= 181), h4's C4=324 (set iff d4 >= 203). f2, h1, h2, h3 have B == 0 identically and need no correction.

So the rewrite stores the uncorrected S in d_out_tmp and applies the -2^17*B correction in stage 3, which in the source carries no logic at all: since the correction touches only bits 19:17, dout = {(d_out_tmp[19:17] - B)[1:0], d_out_tmp[16:3]}. B is carried alongside S by registering the threshold comparisons in stage 1 and a 2-bit count in stage 2, so it arrives with d_out_tmp.

Per module, replace the declarations of q1..q7 and the whole always body (keep clk/din/dout and reg[19:0] d_out_tmp; as they are). Template, shown for fltr_compute_f1 (coefficients 29,101,17,277 from lines 859-865):

verilog
    reg[8:0] s1;                 // din[55:48] + din[7:0]   (C1 == C7 == 29)
    reg[8:0] s2;                 // din[47:40] + din[15:8]  (C2 == C6 == 101)
    reg[8:0] s3;                 // din[39:32] + din[23:16] (C3 == C5 == 17)
    reg[7:0] r4;                 // din[31:24]              (C4 == 277)
    reg b4;                      // q4[16] of the source: d4*277 >= 2^16
    reg[1:0] bcnt;               // that bit, aligned with d_out_tmp
    reg[19:0] d_out_tmp;

    wire[63:0] sop0_out;
    wire[63:0] sop1_out;
    comb_sop_2_18 sop0 (.ax({9'b0, s2}), .ay(19'd101), .bx({10'b0, r4}), .by(19'd277), .result(sop0_out));
    comb_sop_2_18 sop1 (.ax({9'b0, s1}), .ay(19'd29),  .bx({9'b0, s3}),  .by(19'd17),  .result(sop1_out));

    // the source sign-extends each unsigned q_i, worth -2^17 per set MSB; only q4 can set it
    wire[2:0] topc = d_out_tmp[19:17] - {1'b0, bcnt};

    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
        s1 <= din[55:48] + din[7:0];
        s2 <= din[47:40] + din[15:8];
        s3 <= din[39:32] + din[23:16];
        r4 <= din[31:24];
        b4 <= (din[31:24] >= 8'd237);
        bcnt <= {1'b0, b4};
        d_out_tmp <= sop0_out[19:0] + sop1_out[19:0];
        dout <= {topc[1:0], d_out_tmp[16:3]};
    end

The other six follow the same shape; only the block operands, the soft term and the correction differ. Always build the soft terms into a single t_soft wire first and add the block output last, so that exactly one adder level sits between a block output and d_out_tmp:

  • fltr_compute_f2 (lines 889-895: 4,42,163,255) and fltr_compute_h2 (lines 992-998, identical coefficients): one block sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd42),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd163)); wire[19:0] t_c4 = {4'b0, r4, 8'b0} - {12'b0, r4}; (255*r4) wire[19:0] t_soft = t_c4 + {9'b0, s1, 2'b0}; (+ 4*s1) d_out_tmp <= sop0_out[19:0] + t_soft; dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3]; (no correction, no bcnt).
  • fltr_compute_f3 (lines 928-934: 20,179,364, centre 0): one block sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd179),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd364)); wire[19:0] t_soft = {7'b0, s1, 4'b0} + {9'b0, s1, 2'b0}; (20*s1); no r4 at all (the source's q4 is din[31:24]*0); correction b3 <= (din[39:32] >= 8'd181); b5 <= (din[23:16] >= 8'd181); bcnt <= b3 + b5; and dout <= {topc[1:0], d_out_tmp[16:3]};
  • fltr_compute_h1 (lines 959-965: 17,25,193, centre 0): sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd25),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd193)); wire[19:0] t_soft = {7'b0, s1, 4'b0} + {11'b0, s1}; (17*s1); no correction, no r4.
  • fltr_compute_h3 (lines 1030-1036: 23,72,147, centre 0): sop0(.ax({9'b0,s1}),.ay(19'd23),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd147)); wire[19:0] t_soft = {5'b0, s2, 6'b0} + {8'b0, s2, 3'b0}; (72*s2); no correction, no r4.
  • fltr_compute_h4 (lines 1065-1071: 14,43,80,324): sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd43),.bx({10'b0,r4}),.by(19'd324)); wire[19:0] t_c1 = {7'b0, s1, 4'b0} - {10'b0, s1, 1'b0}; (14*s1) wire[19:0] t_c3 = {5'b0, s3, 6'b0} + {7'b0, s3, 4'b0}; (80*s3) wire[19:0] t_soft = t_c1 + t_c3;; correction b4 <= (din[31:24] >= 8'd203); bcnt <= {1'b0, b4}; and the corrected dout.

Every soft term above is a non-negative shift-add of a registered value, every concatenation is exactly 20 bits, and all sums are below 2^20, so the 20-bit arithmetic is exact rather than merely congruent.

No assumption about the design's inputs is needed: there is no ASSUMES: line.

Visibility and X behaviour

In fltr_compute_*, q1..q7 and d_out_tmp are read only by the sum and by dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3] respectively (checked in all seven modules), so nothing that disappears inside a block is read elsewhere; dout is the only module output. The register count on every path is unchanged (din -> 1 register -> sum -> d_out_tmp -> dout), all fltr registers are unconditional, and the equivalence testbench compares from the first cycle after reset while the filter inputs are still flushing X, so X timing must match: it does, because an X on any din byte makes the source's d_out_tmp X (it sums all seven q_i), and makes s1/s2/s3 X here. For f3/h1/h3, where the rewrite stops reading din[31:24] (the source multiplies it by 0, and x*0 is x in Verilog), din[31:24] comes from buff_out4 while din[23:16], din[15:8], din[7:0] come from fifos further down the same chain, so those bytes are X whenever buff_out4 is - the rewritten module is X on exactly the same cycles.

Blocks, tiles, and what is left in soft logic
  • Blocks added: 48 on the my_fir side (my_fir_f1 two, each of the other six modules one, times 6 instances) plus 48 on the fltr side (fltr_compute_f1 two, each of the other six one, times 6 instances) = 96 blocks, each taking a DSP tile alone.
  • After the rewrite no * operator is left anywhere in the design: every remaining coefficient is realised as a shift-add. So the design uses 96 DSP tiles, against 224 in the baseline and 107 in the kept candidate: 11 tiles fewer than the kept candidate (2.8e6 area), and in exchange the six-level 20-bit adder chain plus the 7x17 product registers of all 42 fltr instances leave the soft fabric, replaced per instance by three 9-bit pre-adds, at most three 20-bit shift-adds, one 20-bit combining add and a 3-bit correction.
  • Candidates converted: all 30 fltr ids and all 31 my_fir ids listed in REGIONS - every product that ends up inside a block.

  • Candidates left, grouped by reason - coefficient is a cheap shift-add, so keeping it in soft logic lets the module finish in one block instead of two; moving any of them into a block would buy a second DSP tile per instance (253779 each, about 9 CLBs) without shortening any stage, because they are off the block path and are absorbed by the slack in front of the final adder:

    • fltr_compute_f2 889$58, 895$64 (C=4, one shift) and 892$61 (C=255 = 256-1); fltr_compute_h2 992$100, 998$106, 995$103 (same coefficients);
    • fltr_compute_f3 928$72, 934$78 (C=20 = 16+4); fltr_compute_h1 959$86, 965$92 (C=17 = 16+1); fltr_compute_h3 1031$115, 1035$119 (C=72 = 64+8);
    • fltr_compute_h4 1065$128, 1071$134 (C=14 = 16-2) and 1067$130, 1069$132 (C=80 = 64+16);
    • my_fir_f2 1542$169, 1548$180, 1545$174 and my_fir_h2 1716$210, 1722$221, 1719$215 (COEF0=4, COEF3=255); my_fir_f3 1602$184, 1607$193 (12 = 8+4); my_fir_h1 1661$197, 1666$206 (15 = 16-1); my_fir_h3 1775$225, 1780$234 and my_fir_h4 1833$238, 1838$247 (9 = 8+1).
    • The fltr centre taps of f3, h1 and h3 (coefficient 0) are not candidates and simply vanish, as they already do in the baseline.
Stages and delay

Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. No block feeds another block; on both sides a block output goes through at most one soft adder level into a register. The block path of a fltr stage 2 is 0.06 (clock-to-output) + 1.42 (register to block) + 2.14 (block) + 0.96 (block into soft logic) + one 20-bit adder level + the wire to the flip-flop, i.e. about 7.0 ns at the medians and about 8.0 ns if every wire and the adder come out at the pessimistic end - at or below the 8.202 ns my_fir stage that this rewrite does not touch, and far below the baseline's 11.6069 ns. The soft terms t_soft are at most two adder levels deep from a register (about 4.1 ns), so they are ready before the block output reaches the final adder and never extend the stage; this is why f1, whose four products would need a five-operand three-level soft tree, gets a second block instead and ends with a single sop0+sop1 level. The correction B is deliberately moved into stage 3, where the source has only wires, so it costs no level in stage 2.

Soft logic leaving a stage: the six-level 20-bit adder chain of every fltr_compute instance leaves stage 2 (replaced by one adder level after the block), and the seven 17-bit product registers leave stage 1 (replaced by three 9-bit pre-adds and at most 10 further bits of register). That stage was not the slowest - the slowest stage is the my_fir sum, 8.202 ns - but it was the same shape as the baseline's critical path (one hard multiply then six adder levels), so shortening it carries no risk of a new critical path. Stage 1 of fltr becomes a register-to-register 9-bit add, roughly 3.8 ns. The my_fir stages are unchanged from the kept candidate, so the period should stay at about 8.2 ns.

Register stages, per converted region, operands to result:

  • fltr_compute_* (all 30 converted ids): before - operand byte to product: 1 stage (q_i); product to sum: 1 stage, the sum lands in d_out_tmp; d_out_tmp to dout: 1 stage; three stages in all. After - operand byte to the registered pre-sum s1/s2/s3/r4: 1 stage; the block forms its two products and their sum combinationally in the next stage and lands in d_out_tmp: 0 stages between products and sum; d_out_tmp to dout: 1 stage; three stages in all, so the latency of dout is unchanged and the pipeline depth of the design is unchanged.
  • my_fir_* (all 31 converted ids): before - 0 register stages between the products and the sum, both in the stage that writes dout. After - unchanged at 0: the pre-add, the block's products and the final sum are all in the stage that writes dout.

No register is added, moved or removed on the my_fir side; on the fltr side the stage-1 registers change shape (q1..q7 become s1,s2,s3[,r4,b]) but stay in the same stage with the same unconditional clocking, and the added b/bcnt bits do not rely on their initial value: they are X exactly when the data they qualify is X.

DESIGN_CHANGE: each of the six fltr groups drives its seven fltr_compute_* instances with one and the same 56-bit din (lines 824-830), so the three 9-bit pre-sums s1,s2,s3 are computed seven times over per group. Hoisting them into the parent and passing the registered pre-sums (plus din, which fltr_compute_f3/h4/f1 still need for their threshold bits) into the children would delete about 126 of the 9-bit adders and their registers, roughly 100 clusters, at the cost of changing the child port lists - a change to the design, not to the rewrite, so it is not part of this plan.

1	// comb_sop_2_18: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx*by, all four operands unsigned
2	// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); each 18x19 product is 37
3	// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
4	// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
5	// Ports: ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every
6	// input reaches result in the same cycle.
7	module comb_sop_2_18 (
8	    input  [17:0] ax,
9	    input  [18:0] ay,
10	    input  [17:0] bx,
11	    input  [18:0] by,
12	    output [63:0] result
13	);
14	
15	    wire [36:0] prod_a = ax * ay;                                    // 18x19 -> 37, exact
16	    wire [36:0] prod_b = bx * by;                                    // 18x19 -> 37, exact
17	    wire [63:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b;                            // zero-extended, exact
18	
19	    assign result = sum;
20	
21	endmodule

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Check
  • Every claim the plan makes about the design (who reads a value, a register's reset or enable, widths, cited lines, ASSUMES lines) against the source.
  • That the mapping as described keeps the same behavior.
  • That the plan states everything the planner's output section requires, listed below.

Do not judge cost or style; measurement decides cost.

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output
  • First line exactly APPROVE or REVISE.
  • If REVISE, for each problem: the rule it violates or the required item it omits, by name; the design lines; what to change.
  • Write nothing before the verdict line; read the source first. The verdict is applied automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.

(B) fltr_compute_* (new): taps d1=din[55:48], d2=din[47:40], d3=din[39:32], d4=din[31:24], d5=din[23:16], d6=din[15:8], d7=din[7:0], all 8-bit unsigned; every fltr coefficient set is symmetric (C7==C1, C6==C2, C5==C3), so the registers q1..q7 are replaced by the registered 9-bit pre-sums s1 <= din[55:48]+din[7:0]; s2 <= din[47:40]+din[15:8]; s3 <= din[39:32]+din[23:16]; plus r4 <= din[31:24] where C4!=0. Block ports per module: f1 sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd101),.bx({10'b0,r4}),.by(19'd277)) and sop1(.ax({9'b0,s1}),.ay(19'd29),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd17)); f2 and h2 sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd42),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd163)); f3 sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd179),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd364)); h1 sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd25),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd193)); h3 sop0(.ax({9'b0,s1}),.ay(19'd23),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd147)); h4 sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd43),.bx({10'b0,r4}),.by(19'd324)). Every block port is connected; no product-term port is unused, so none is tied to 0.
PLAN:

What this plan is

It keeps the kept candidate's my_fir rewrite exactly as measured (48 blocks, period 8.202 ns at seed 1) and adds the same treatment to the seven fltr_compute_* modules, which the kept candidate left entirely alone. The fltr side is where the remaining soft arithmetic of this design sits: 42 instances (7 modules x 6), each a seven-tap symmetric FIR whose 7 registered products are summed by a six-level chain of 20-bit adders. That chain disappears; the 57-59 mult_9x9 tiles that hold the fltr products are replaced by 48 blocks. The period is set by the my_fir stage and is untouched; the gain is area and wirelength.

Apply both parts to the unmodified stereovision2.v in this directory.

Part A - my_fir_* (reproduce the kept candidate verbatim)

In every my_fir_* module insert, before the always block:

verilog
	// symmetric taps pre-added: COEF6==COEF0, COEF5==COEF1, COEF4==COEF2
	wire[16:0] s0 = din + n_delay_reg6;
	wire[16:0] s1 = n_delay_reg1 + n_delay_reg5;
	wire[16:0] s2 = n_delay_reg2 + n_delay_reg4;

and the localparams/blocks/soft terms below; replace only the dout <= ... sum inside if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1), leaving the delay-line shifts, output_data_ready and the else branch alone.

  • my_fir_f1 (_b, 29,101,15,235,15,101,29): localparam[18:0] C0=COEF0_b, C1=COEF1_b, C2=COEF2_b, C3=COEF3_b; two blocks, sop0(.ax({1'b0,s0}),.ay(C0),.bx({1'b0,s1}),.by(C1),.result(sop0_out)), sop1(.ax({1'b0,s2}),.ay(C2),.bx({2'b0,n_delay_reg3}),.by(C3),.result(sop1_out)), and dout <= sop0_out[27:0] + sop1_out[27:0];
  • my_fir_f2 (_c) and my_fir_h2 (_2): one block on C1,C2 as in MAPPING; wire[27:0] t255 = {n_delay_reg3, 8'b0} - n_delay_reg3; wire[27:0] t_soft = t255 + {s0, 2'b0}; dout <= sop0_out[27:0] + t_soft; (COEF3==255 and COEF0==4 stay soft shifts)
  • my_fir_f3 (_d): one block on C1,C2; wire[27:0] t_soft = {s0, 3'b0} + {s0, 2'b0}; (COEF0==12)
  • my_fir_h1 (_1): one block on C1,C2; wire[27:0] t_soft = {s0, 4'b0} - s0; (COEF0==15)
  • my_fir_h3 (_3) and my_fir_h4 (_4): one block on C1,C2; wire[27:0] t_soft = {s0, 3'b0} + s0; (COEF0==9)

All seven coefficient sets of my_fir are below 258 and all sums fit the 28-bit dout (largest 673*65535 = 4.4e7 < 2^28), so the regrouping is bit-exact; this part is already confirmed by the reference simulation of the kept candidate.

Part B - fltr_compute_* (new)

Each fltr_compute_* module is

q_i <= d_i * C_i                                  (stage 1)
d_out_tmp <= sum of sign_extend20(q_i)            (stage 2, six adder levels)
dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3]                           (stage 3, wires only)

with C7==C1, C6==C2, C5==C3 in all seven modules, so the 7 products are 4 distinct products of the pre-sums s1=d1+d7, s2=d2+d6, s3=d3+d5 and the centre tap d4.

Two facts make the regrouping exact:

  1. Each q_i is 17 bits and no product of this design overflows 17 bits (largest is 255*364 = 92820), and the true sum S = sum_i(d_i*C_i) never reaches 2^20 (largest module total 510*563 = 287130 for f3), so S may be formed at 20 bits with no wrap, and the pair products (d1+d7)*C1 etc. are exact.
  2. The source sign-extends each unsigned q_i by replicating q_i[16] into bits 19:17, which is worth -2^17*q_i[16] modulo 2^20. So the register the source writes is d_out_tmp = S - 2^17*B (mod 2^20), with B = sum_i q_i[16]. q_i[16] can only be 1 when 255*C_i >= 65536, i.e. C_i >= 258; that happens for exactly three coefficients in the whole design: f1's C4=277 (set iff d4 >= 237), f3's C3=C5=364 (set iff d3 >= 181, resp. d5 >= 181), h4's C4=324 (set iff d4 >= 203). f2, h1, h2, h3 have B == 0 identically and need no correction.

So the rewrite stores the uncorrected S in d_out_tmp and applies the -2^17*B correction in stage 3, which in the source carries no logic at all: since the correction touches only bits 19:17, dout = {(d_out_tmp[19:17] - B)[1:0], d_out_tmp[16:3]}. B is carried alongside S by registering the threshold comparisons in stage 1 and a 2-bit count in stage 2, so it arrives with d_out_tmp.

Per module, replace the declarations of q1..q7 and the whole always body (keep clk/din/dout and reg[19:0] d_out_tmp; as they are). Template, shown for fltr_compute_f1 (coefficients 29,101,17,277 from lines 859-865):

verilog
    reg[8:0] s1;                 // din[55:48] + din[7:0]   (C1 == C7 == 29)
    reg[8:0] s2;                 // din[47:40] + din[15:8]  (C2 == C6 == 101)
    reg[8:0] s3;                 // din[39:32] + din[23:16] (C3 == C5 == 17)
    reg[7:0] r4;                 // din[31:24]              (C4 == 277)
    reg b4;                      // q4[16] of the source: d4*277 >= 2^16
    reg[1:0] bcnt;               // that bit, aligned with d_out_tmp
    reg[19:0] d_out_tmp;

    wire[63:0] sop0_out;
    wire[63:0] sop1_out;
    comb_sop_2_18 sop0 (.ax({9'b0, s2}), .ay(19'd101), .bx({10'b0, r4}), .by(19'd277), .result(sop0_out));
    comb_sop_2_18 sop1 (.ax({9'b0, s1}), .ay(19'd29),  .bx({9'b0, s3}),  .by(19'd17),  .result(sop1_out));

    // the source sign-extends each unsigned q_i, worth -2^17 per set MSB; only q4 can set it
    wire[2:0] topc = d_out_tmp[19:17] - {1'b0, bcnt};

    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
        s1 <= din[55:48] + din[7:0];
        s2 <= din[47:40] + din[15:8];
        s3 <= din[39:32] + din[23:16];
        r4 <= din[31:24];
        b4 <= (din[31:24] >= 8'd237);
        bcnt <= {1'b0, b4};
        d_out_tmp <= sop0_out[19:0] + sop1_out[19:0];
        dout <= {topc[1:0], d_out_tmp[16:3]};
    end

The other six follow the same shape; only the block operands, the soft term and the correction differ. Always build the soft terms into a single t_soft wire first and add the block output last, so that exactly one adder level sits between a block output and d_out_tmp:

  • fltr_compute_f2 (lines 889-895: 4,42,163,255) and fltr_compute_h2 (lines 992-998, identical coefficients): one block sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd42),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd163)); wire[19:0] t_c4 = {4'b0, r4, 8'b0} - {12'b0, r4}; (255*r4) wire[19:0] t_soft = t_c4 + {9'b0, s1, 2'b0}; (+ 4*s1) d_out_tmp <= sop0_out[19:0] + t_soft; dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3]; (no correction, no bcnt).
  • fltr_compute_f3 (lines 928-934: 20,179,364, centre 0): one block sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd179),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd364)); wire[19:0] t_soft = {7'b0, s1, 4'b0} + {9'b0, s1, 2'b0}; (20*s1); no r4 at all (the source's q4 is din[31:24]*0); correction b3 <= (din[39:32] >= 8'd181); b5 <= (din[23:16] >= 8'd181); bcnt <= b3 + b5; and dout <= {topc[1:0], d_out_tmp[16:3]};
  • fltr_compute_h1 (lines 959-965: 17,25,193, centre 0): sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd25),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd193)); wire[19:0] t_soft = {7'b0, s1, 4'b0} + {11'b0, s1}; (17*s1); no correction, no r4.
  • fltr_compute_h3 (lines 1030-1036: 23,72,147, centre 0): sop0(.ax({9'b0,s1}),.ay(19'd23),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd147)); wire[19:0] t_soft = {5'b0, s2, 6'b0} + {8'b0, s2, 3'b0}; (72*s2); no correction, no r4.
  • fltr_compute_h4 (lines 1065-1071: 14,43,80,324): sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd43),.bx({10'b0,r4}),.by(19'd324)); wire[19:0] t_c1 = {7'b0, s1, 4'b0} - {10'b0, s1, 1'b0}; (14*s1) wire[19:0] t_c3 = {5'b0, s3, 6'b0} + {7'b0, s3, 4'b0}; (80*s3) wire[19:0] t_soft = t_c1 + t_c3;; correction b4 <= (din[31:24] >= 8'd203); bcnt <= {1'b0, b4}; and the corrected dout.

Every soft term above is a non-negative shift-add of a registered value, every concatenation is exactly 20 bits, and all sums are below 2^20, so the 20-bit arithmetic is exact rather than merely congruent.

No assumption about the design's inputs is needed: there is no ASSUMES: line.

Visibility and X behaviour

In fltr_compute_*, q1..q7 and d_out_tmp are read only by the sum and by dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3] respectively (checked in all seven modules), so nothing that disappears inside a block is read elsewhere; dout is the only module output. The register count on every path is unchanged (din -> 1 register -> sum -> d_out_tmp -> dout), all fltr registers are unconditional, and the equivalence testbench compares from the first cycle after reset while the filter inputs are still flushing X, so X timing must match: it does, because an X on any din byte makes the source's d_out_tmp X (it sums all seven q_i), and makes s1/s2/s3 X here. For f3/h1/h3, where the rewrite stops reading din[31:24] (the source multiplies it by 0, and x*0 is x in Verilog), din[31:24] comes from buff_out4 while din[23:16], din[15:8], din[7:0] come from fifos further down the same chain, so those bytes are X whenever buff_out4 is - the rewritten module is X on exactly the same cycles.

Blocks, tiles, and what is left in soft logic
  • Blocks added: 48 on the my_fir side (my_fir_f1 two, each of the other six modules one, times 6 instances) plus 48 on the fltr side (fltr_compute_f1 two, each of the other six one, times 6 instances) = 96 blocks, each taking a DSP tile alone.
  • After the rewrite no * operator is left anywhere in the design: every remaining coefficient is realised as a shift-add. So the design uses 96 DSP tiles, against 224 in the baseline and 107 in the kept candidate: 11 tiles fewer than the kept candidate (2.8e6 area), and in exchange the six-level 20-bit adder chain plus the 7x17 product registers of all 42 fltr instances leave the soft fabric, replaced per instance by three 9-bit pre-adds, at most three 20-bit shift-adds, one 20-bit combining add and a 3-bit correction.
  • Candidates converted: all 30 fltr ids and all 31 my_fir ids listed in REGIONS - every product that ends up inside a block.

  • Candidates left, grouped by reason - coefficient is a cheap shift-add, so keeping it in soft logic lets the module finish in one block instead of two; moving any of them into a block would buy a second DSP tile per instance (253779 each, about 9 CLBs) without shortening any stage, because they are off the block path and are absorbed by the slack in front of the final adder:

    • fltr_compute_f2 889$58, 895$64 (C=4, one shift) and 892$61 (C=255 = 256-1); fltr_compute_h2 992$100, 998$106, 995$103 (same coefficients);
    • fltr_compute_f3 928$72, 934$78 (C=20 = 16+4); fltr_compute_h1 959$86, 965$92 (C=17 = 16+1); fltr_compute_h3 1031$115, 1035$119 (C=72 = 64+8);
    • fltr_compute_h4 1065$128, 1071$134 (C=14 = 16-2) and 1067$130, 1069$132 (C=80 = 64+16);
    • my_fir_f2 1542$169, 1548$180, 1545$174 and my_fir_h2 1716$210, 1722$221, 1719$215 (COEF0=4, COEF3=255); my_fir_f3 1602$184, 1607$193 (12 = 8+4); my_fir_h1 1661$197, 1666$206 (15 = 16-1); my_fir_h3 1775$225, 1780$234 and my_fir_h4 1833$238, 1838$247 (9 = 8+1).
    • The fltr centre taps of f3, h1 and h3 (coefficient 0) are not candidates and simply vanish, as they already do in the baseline.
Stages and delay

Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. No block feeds another block; on both sides a block output goes through at most one soft adder level into a register. The block path of a fltr stage 2 is 0.06 (clock-to-output) + 1.42 (register to block) + 2.14 (block) + 0.96 (block into soft logic) + one 20-bit adder level + the wire to the flip-flop, i.e. about 7.0 ns at the medians and about 8.0 ns if every wire and the adder come out at the pessimistic end - at or below the 8.202 ns my_fir stage that this rewrite does not touch, and far below the baseline's 11.6069 ns. The soft terms t_soft are at most two adder levels deep from a register (about 4.1 ns), so they are ready before the block output reaches the final adder and never extend the stage; this is why f1, whose four products would need a five-operand three-level soft tree, gets a second block instead and ends with a single sop0+sop1 level. The correction B is deliberately moved into stage 3, where the source has only wires, so it costs no level in stage 2.

Soft logic leaving a stage: the six-level 20-bit adder chain of every fltr_compute instance leaves stage 2 (replaced by one adder level after the block), and the seven 17-bit product registers leave stage 1 (replaced by three 9-bit pre-adds and at most 10 further bits of register). That stage was not the slowest - the slowest stage is the my_fir sum, 8.202 ns - but it was the same shape as the baseline's critical path (one hard multiply then six adder levels), so shortening it carries no risk of a new critical path. Stage 1 of fltr becomes a register-to-register 9-bit add, roughly 3.8 ns. The my_fir stages are unchanged from the kept candidate, so the period should stay at about 8.2 ns.

Register stages, per converted region, operands to result:

  • fltr_compute_* (all 30 converted ids): before - operand byte to product: 1 stage (q_i); product to sum: 1 stage, the sum lands in d_out_tmp; d_out_tmp to dout: 1 stage; three stages in all. After - operand byte to the registered pre-sum s1/s2/s3/r4: 1 stage; the block forms its two products and their sum combinationally in the next stage and lands in d_out_tmp: 0 stages between products and sum; d_out_tmp to dout: 1 stage; three stages in all, so the latency of dout is unchanged and the pipeline depth of the design is unchanged.
  • my_fir_* (all 31 converted ids): before - 0 register stages between the products and the sum, both in the stage that writes dout. After - unchanged at 0: the pre-add, the block's products and the final sum are all in the stage that writes dout.

No register is added, moved or removed on the my_fir side; on the fltr side the stage-1 registers change shape (q1..q7 become s1,s2,s3[,r4,b]) but stay in the same stage with the same unconditional clocking, and the added b/bcnt bits do not rely on their initial value: they are X exactly when the data they qualify is X.

DESIGN_CHANGE: each of the six fltr groups drives its seven fltr_compute_* instances with one and the same 56-bit din (lines 824-830), so the three 9-bit pre-sums s1,s2,s3 are computed seven times over per group. Hoisting them into the parent and passing the registered pre-sums (plus din, which fltr_compute_f3/h4/f1 still need for their threshold bits) into the children would delete about 126 of the 9-bit adders and their registers, roughly 100 clusters, at the cost of changing the child port lists - a change to the design, not to the rewrite, so it is not part of this plan.

Reference simulation

After the edit, the framework simulates the edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle. A candidate that does not match is not measured. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (comb_sop_2_18.v) are in sim_reference/.

  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.

PLAN:

What this plan is

It keeps the kept candidate's my_fir rewrite exactly as measured (48 blocks, period 8.202 ns at seed 1) and adds the same treatment to the seven fltr_compute_* modules, which the kept candidate left entirely alone. The fltr side is where the remaining soft arithmetic of this design sits: 42 instances (7 modules x 6), each a seven-tap symmetric FIR whose 7 registered products are summed by a six-level chain of 20-bit adders. That chain disappears; the 57-59 mult_9x9 tiles that hold the fltr products are replaced by 48 blocks. The period is set by the my_fir stage and is untouched; the gain is area and wirelength.

Apply both parts to the unmodified stereovision2.v in this directory.

Part A - my_fir_* (reproduce the kept candidate verbatim)

In every my_fir_* module insert, before the always block:

verilog
	// symmetric taps pre-added: COEF6==COEF0, COEF5==COEF1, COEF4==COEF2
	wire[16:0] s0 = din + n_delay_reg6;
	wire[16:0] s1 = n_delay_reg1 + n_delay_reg5;
	wire[16:0] s2 = n_delay_reg2 + n_delay_reg4;

and the localparams/blocks/soft terms below; replace only the dout <= ... sum inside if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1), leaving the delay-line shifts, output_data_ready and the else branch alone.

  • my_fir_f1 (_b, 29,101,15,235,15,101,29): localparam[18:0] C0=COEF0_b, C1=COEF1_b, C2=COEF2_b, C3=COEF3_b; two blocks, sop0(.ax({1'b0,s0}),.ay(C0),.bx({1'b0,s1}),.by(C1),.result(sop0_out)), sop1(.ax({1'b0,s2}),.ay(C2),.bx({2'b0,n_delay_reg3}),.by(C3),.result(sop1_out)), and dout <= sop0_out[27:0] + sop1_out[27:0];
  • my_fir_f2 (_c) and my_fir_h2 (_2): one block on C1,C2 as in MAPPING; wire[27:0] t255 = {n_delay_reg3, 8'b0} - n_delay_reg3; wire[27:0] t_soft = t255 + {s0, 2'b0}; dout <= sop0_out[27:0] + t_soft; (COEF3==255 and COEF0==4 stay soft shifts)
  • my_fir_f3 (_d): one block on C1,C2; wire[27:0] t_soft = {s0, 3'b0} + {s0, 2'b0}; (COEF0==12)
  • my_fir_h1 (_1): one block on C1,C2; wire[27:0] t_soft = {s0, 4'b0} - s0; (COEF0==15)
  • my_fir_h3 (_3) and my_fir_h4 (_4): one block on C1,C2; wire[27:0] t_soft = {s0, 3'b0} + s0; (COEF0==9)

All seven coefficient sets of my_fir are below 258 and all sums fit the 28-bit dout (largest 673*65535 = 4.4e7 < 2^28), so the regrouping is bit-exact; this part is already confirmed by the reference simulation of the kept candidate.

Part B - fltr_compute_* (new)

Each fltr_compute_* module is

q_i <= d_i * C_i                                  (stage 1)
d_out_tmp <= sum of sign_extend20(q_i)            (stage 2, six adder levels)
dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3]                           (stage 3, wires only)

with C7==C1, C6==C2, C5==C3 in all seven modules, so the 7 products are 4 distinct products of the pre-sums s1=d1+d7, s2=d2+d6, s3=d3+d5 and the centre tap d4.

Two facts make the regrouping exact:

  1. Each q_i is 17 bits and no product of this design overflows 17 bits (largest is 255*364 = 92820), and the true sum S = sum_i(d_i*C_i) never reaches 2^20 (largest module total 510*563 = 287130 for f3), so S may be formed at 20 bits with no wrap, and the pair products (d1+d7)*C1 etc. are exact.
  2. The source sign-extends each unsigned q_i by replicating q_i[16] into bits 19:17, which is worth -2^17*q_i[16] modulo 2^20. So the register the source writes is d_out_tmp = S - 2^17*B (mod 2^20), with B = sum_i q_i[16]. q_i[16] can only be 1 when 255*C_i >= 65536, i.e. C_i >= 258; that happens for exactly three coefficients in the whole design: f1's C4=277 (set iff d4 >= 237), f3's C3=C5=364 (set iff d3 >= 181, resp. d5 >= 181), h4's C4=324 (set iff d4 >= 203). f2, h1, h2, h3 have B == 0 identically and need no correction.

So the rewrite stores the uncorrected S in d_out_tmp and applies the -2^17*B correction in stage 3, which in the source carries no logic at all: since the correction touches only bits 19:17, dout = {(d_out_tmp[19:17] - B)[1:0], d_out_tmp[16:3]}. B is carried alongside S by registering the threshold comparisons in stage 1 and a 2-bit count in stage 2, so it arrives with d_out_tmp.

Per module, replace the declarations of q1..q7 and the whole always body (keep clk/din/dout and reg[19:0] d_out_tmp; as they are). Template, shown for fltr_compute_f1 (coefficients 29,101,17,277 from lines 859-865):

verilog
    reg[8:0] s1;                 // din[55:48] + din[7:0]   (C1 == C7 == 29)
    reg[8:0] s2;                 // din[47:40] + din[15:8]  (C2 == C6 == 101)
    reg[8:0] s3;                 // din[39:32] + din[23:16] (C3 == C5 == 17)
    reg[7:0] r4;                 // din[31:24]              (C4 == 277)
    reg b4;                      // q4[16] of the source: d4*277 >= 2^16
    reg[1:0] bcnt;               // that bit, aligned with d_out_tmp
    reg[19:0] d_out_tmp;

    wire[63:0] sop0_out;
    wire[63:0] sop1_out;
    comb_sop_2_18 sop0 (.ax({9'b0, s2}), .ay(19'd101), .bx({10'b0, r4}), .by(19'd277), .result(sop0_out));
    comb_sop_2_18 sop1 (.ax({9'b0, s1}), .ay(19'd29),  .bx({9'b0, s3}),  .by(19'd17),  .result(sop1_out));

    // the source sign-extends each unsigned q_i, worth -2^17 per set MSB; only q4 can set it
    wire[2:0] topc = d_out_tmp[19:17] - {1'b0, bcnt};

    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
        s1 <= din[55:48] + din[7:0];
        s2 <= din[47:40] + din[15:8];
        s3 <= din[39:32] + din[23:16];
        r4 <= din[31:24];
        b4 <= (din[31:24] >= 8'd237);
        bcnt <= {1'b0, b4};
        d_out_tmp <= sop0_out[19:0] + sop1_out[19:0];
        dout <= {topc[1:0], d_out_tmp[16:3]};
    end

The other six follow the same shape; only the block operands, the soft term and the correction differ. Always build the soft terms into a single t_soft wire first and add the block output last, so that exactly one adder level sits between a block output and d_out_tmp:

  • fltr_compute_f2 (lines 889-895: 4,42,163,255) and fltr_compute_h2 (lines 992-998, identical coefficients): one block sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd42),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd163)); wire[19:0] t_c4 = {4'b0, r4, 8'b0} - {12'b0, r4}; (255*r4) wire[19:0] t_soft = t_c4 + {9'b0, s1, 2'b0}; (+ 4*s1) d_out_tmp <= sop0_out[19:0] + t_soft; dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3]; (no correction, no bcnt).
  • fltr_compute_f3 (lines 928-934: 20,179,364, centre 0): one block sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd179),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd364)); wire[19:0] t_soft = {7'b0, s1, 4'b0} + {9'b0, s1, 2'b0}; (20*s1); no r4 at all (the source's q4 is din[31:24]*0); correction b3 <= (din[39:32] >= 8'd181); b5 <= (din[23:16] >= 8'd181); bcnt <= b3 + b5; and dout <= {topc[1:0], d_out_tmp[16:3]};
  • fltr_compute_h1 (lines 959-965: 17,25,193, centre 0): sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd25),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd193)); wire[19:0] t_soft = {7'b0, s1, 4'b0} + {11'b0, s1}; (17*s1); no correction, no r4.
  • fltr_compute_h3 (lines 1030-1036: 23,72,147, centre 0): sop0(.ax({9'b0,s1}),.ay(19'd23),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd147)); wire[19:0] t_soft = {5'b0, s2, 6'b0} + {8'b0, s2, 3'b0}; (72*s2); no correction, no r4.
  • fltr_compute_h4 (lines 1065-1071: 14,43,80,324): sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd43),.bx({10'b0,r4}),.by(19'd324)); wire[19:0] t_c1 = {7'b0, s1, 4'b0} - {10'b0, s1, 1'b0}; (14*s1) wire[19:0] t_c3 = {5'b0, s3, 6'b0} + {7'b0, s3, 4'b0}; (80*s3) wire[19:0] t_soft = t_c1 + t_c3;; correction b4 <= (din[31:24] >= 8'd203); bcnt <= {1'b0, b4}; and the corrected dout.

Every soft term above is a non-negative shift-add of a registered value, every concatenation is exactly 20 bits, and all sums are below 2^20, so the 20-bit arithmetic is exact rather than merely congruent.

No assumption about the design's inputs is needed: there is no ASSUMES: line.

Visibility and X behaviour

In fltr_compute_*, q1..q7 and d_out_tmp are read only by the sum and by dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3] respectively (checked in all seven modules), so nothing that disappears inside a block is read elsewhere; dout is the only module output. The register count on every path is unchanged (din -> 1 register -> sum -> d_out_tmp -> dout), all fltr registers are unconditional, and the equivalence testbench compares from the first cycle after reset while the filter inputs are still flushing X, so X timing must match: it does, because an X on any din byte makes the source's d_out_tmp X (it sums all seven q_i), and makes s1/s2/s3 X here. For f3/h1/h3, where the rewrite stops reading din[31:24] (the source multiplies it by 0, and x*0 is x in Verilog), din[31:24] comes from buff_out4 while din[23:16], din[15:8], din[7:0] come from fifos further down the same chain, so those bytes are X whenever buff_out4 is - the rewritten module is X on exactly the same cycles.

Blocks, tiles, and what is left in soft logic
  • Blocks added: 48 on the my_fir side (my_fir_f1 two, each of the other six modules one, times 6 instances) plus 48 on the fltr side (fltr_compute_f1 two, each of the other six one, times 6 instances) = 96 blocks, each taking a DSP tile alone.
  • After the rewrite no * operator is left anywhere in the design: every remaining coefficient is realised as a shift-add. So the design uses 96 DSP tiles, against 224 in the baseline and 107 in the kept candidate: 11 tiles fewer than the kept candidate (2.8e6 area), and in exchange the six-level 20-bit adder chain plus the 7x17 product registers of all 42 fltr instances leave the soft fabric, replaced per instance by three 9-bit pre-adds, at most three 20-bit shift-adds, one 20-bit combining add and a 3-bit correction.
  • Candidates converted: all 30 fltr ids and all 31 my_fir ids listed in REGIONS - every product that ends up inside a block.

  • Candidates left, grouped by reason - coefficient is a cheap shift-add, so keeping it in soft logic lets the module finish in one block instead of two; moving any of them into a block would buy a second DSP tile per instance (253779 each, about 9 CLBs) without shortening any stage, because they are off the block path and are absorbed by the slack in front of the final adder:

    • fltr_compute_f2 889$58, 895$64 (C=4, one shift) and 892$61 (C=255 = 256-1); fltr_compute_h2 992$100, 998$106, 995$103 (same coefficients);
    • fltr_compute_f3 928$72, 934$78 (C=20 = 16+4); fltr_compute_h1 959$86, 965$92 (C=17 = 16+1); fltr_compute_h3 1031$115, 1035$119 (C=72 = 64+8);
    • fltr_compute_h4 1065$128, 1071$134 (C=14 = 16-2) and 1067$130, 1069$132 (C=80 = 64+16);
    • my_fir_f2 1542$169, 1548$180, 1545$174 and my_fir_h2 1716$210, 1722$221, 1719$215 (COEF0=4, COEF3=255); my_fir_f3 1602$184, 1607$193 (12 = 8+4); my_fir_h1 1661$197, 1666$206 (15 = 16-1); my_fir_h3 1775$225, 1780$234 and my_fir_h4 1833$238, 1838$247 (9 = 8+1).
    • The fltr centre taps of f3, h1 and h3 (coefficient 0) are not candidates and simply vanish, as they already do in the baseline.
Stages and delay

Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. No block feeds another block; on both sides a block output goes through at most one soft adder level into a register. The block path of a fltr stage 2 is 0.06 (clock-to-output) + 1.42 (register to block) + 2.14 (block) + 0.96 (block into soft logic) + one 20-bit adder level + the wire to the flip-flop, i.e. about 7.0 ns at the medians and about 8.0 ns if every wire and the adder come out at the pessimistic end - at or below the 8.202 ns my_fir stage that this rewrite does not touch, and far below the baseline's 11.6069 ns. The soft terms t_soft are at most two adder levels deep from a register (about 4.1 ns), so they are ready before the block output reaches the final adder and never extend the stage; this is why f1, whose four products would need a five-operand three-level soft tree, gets a second block instead and ends with a single sop0+sop1 level. The correction B is deliberately moved into stage 3, where the source has only wires, so it costs no level in stage 2.

Soft logic leaving a stage: the six-level 20-bit adder chain of every fltr_compute instance leaves stage 2 (replaced by one adder level after the block), and the seven 17-bit product registers leave stage 1 (replaced by three 9-bit pre-adds and at most 10 further bits of register). That stage was not the slowest - the slowest stage is the my_fir sum, 8.202 ns - but it was the same shape as the baseline's critical path (one hard multiply then six adder levels), so shortening it carries no risk of a new critical path. Stage 1 of fltr becomes a register-to-register 9-bit add, roughly 3.8 ns. The my_fir stages are unchanged from the kept candidate, so the period should stay at about 8.2 ns.

Register stages, per converted region, operands to result:

  • fltr_compute_* (all 30 converted ids): before - operand byte to product: 1 stage (q_i); product to sum: 1 stage, the sum lands in d_out_tmp; d_out_tmp to dout: 1 stage; three stages in all. After - operand byte to the registered pre-sum s1/s2/s3/r4: 1 stage; the block forms its two products and their sum combinationally in the next stage and lands in d_out_tmp: 0 stages between products and sum; d_out_tmp to dout: 1 stage; three stages in all, so the latency of dout is unchanged and the pipeline depth of the design is unchanged.
  • my_fir_* (all 31 converted ids): before - 0 register stages between the products and the sum, both in the stage that writes dout. After - unchanged at 0: the pre-add, the block's products and the final sum are all in the stage that writes dout.

No register is added, moved or removed on the my_fir side; on the fltr side the stage-1 registers change shape (q1..q7 become s1,s2,s3[,r4,b]) but stay in the same stage with the same unconditional clocking, and the added b/bcnt bits do not rely on their initial value: they are X exactly when the data they qualify is X.

Simulation

When you finish, the framework simulates your edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle, on its own copy. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (comb_sop_2_18.v) are in sim_reference/; you may read them, but editing them has no effect on the result.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Inner-loop check: the front end of the real flow, then a cell census. NOT place-and-route.
# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
# Reads, in the flow's order: blocks.vlib (every hard block of the architecture, declared from its
# models), primitives.vlib (the flow's library of memories, adders and multipliers), then the design;
# then elaborates with the flow's hierarchy check. A module that is not defined, a port name the
# block does not have, or a misspelled block name fails here as it would in the flow. Do not
# declare the target block in the design: blocks.vlib declares it, and a design that defines a module
# of the target block's name fails this check.
# Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole design (the last "Number of cells"
# table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub, registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as
# $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated module by name, which is where a hard-block
# instantiation shows up with its instance count.
set -u
f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
lib=""
[ -f "$here/blocks.vlib" ] && lib="read_verilog -lib $here/blocks.vlib; "
[ -f "$here/primitives.vlib" ] && lib="${lib}read_verilog -nomem2reg $here/primitives.vlib; "
target="$(sed -n 's|^// target block: *\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*\).*|\1|p' "$here/blocks.vlib" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
if [ -n "$target" ] && grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*module[[:space:]]+$target([^A-Za-z0-9_$]|$)" "$f"; then
  echo "FAIL: $f defines module $target; blocks.vlib declares it. Remove the module definition and keep the instances."
  exit 1
fi
out="$(yosys -p "${lib}read_verilog -sv -nolatches $f; hierarchy -check -auto-top -purge_lib; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
  echo "$out" | tail -10
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
                   on {on=0}
                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true

// comb_sop_2_18: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx*by, all four operands unsigned
// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); each 18x19 product is 37
// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
// Ports: ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every
// input reaches result in the same cycle.
module comb_sop_2_18 (
    input  [17:0] ax,
    input  [18:0] ay,
    input  [17:0] bx,
    input  [18:0] by,
    output [63:0] result
);

    wire [36:0] prod_a = ax * ay;                                    // 18x19 -> 37, exact
    wire [36:0] prod_b = bx * by;                                    // 18x19 -> 37, exact
    wire [63:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b;                            // zero-extended, exact

    assign result = sum;

endmodule

PLAN:

What this plan is

It keeps the kept candidate's my_fir rewrite exactly as measured (48 blocks, period 8.202 ns at seed 1) and adds the same treatment to the seven fltr_compute_* modules, which the kept candidate left entirely alone. The fltr side is where the remaining soft arithmetic of this design sits: 42 instances (7 modules x 6), each a seven-tap symmetric FIR whose 7 registered products are summed by a six-level chain of 20-bit adders. That chain disappears; the 57-59 mult_9x9 tiles that hold the fltr products are replaced by 48 blocks. The period is set by the my_fir stage and is untouched; the gain is area and wirelength.

Apply both parts to the unmodified stereovision2.v in this directory.

Part A - my_fir_* (reproduce the kept candidate verbatim)

In every my_fir_* module insert, before the always block:

verilog
	// symmetric taps pre-added: COEF6==COEF0, COEF5==COEF1, COEF4==COEF2
	wire[16:0] s0 = din + n_delay_reg6;
	wire[16:0] s1 = n_delay_reg1 + n_delay_reg5;
	wire[16:0] s2 = n_delay_reg2 + n_delay_reg4;

and the localparams/blocks/soft terms below; replace only the dout <= ... sum inside if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1), leaving the delay-line shifts, output_data_ready and the else branch alone.

  • my_fir_f1 (_b, 29,101,15,235,15,101,29): localparam[18:0] C0=COEF0_b, C1=COEF1_b, C2=COEF2_b, C3=COEF3_b; two blocks, sop0(.ax({1'b0,s0}),.ay(C0),.bx({1'b0,s1}),.by(C1),.result(sop0_out)), sop1(.ax({1'b0,s2}),.ay(C2),.bx({2'b0,n_delay_reg3}),.by(C3),.result(sop1_out)), and dout <= sop0_out[27:0] + sop1_out[27:0];
  • my_fir_f2 (_c) and my_fir_h2 (_2): one block on C1,C2 as in MAPPING; wire[27:0] t255 = {n_delay_reg3, 8'b0} - n_delay_reg3; wire[27:0] t_soft = t255 + {s0, 2'b0}; dout <= sop0_out[27:0] + t_soft; (COEF3==255 and COEF0==4 stay soft shifts)
  • my_fir_f3 (_d): one block on C1,C2; wire[27:0] t_soft = {s0, 3'b0} + {s0, 2'b0}; (COEF0==12)
  • my_fir_h1 (_1): one block on C1,C2; wire[27:0] t_soft = {s0, 4'b0} - s0; (COEF0==15)
  • my_fir_h3 (_3) and my_fir_h4 (_4): one block on C1,C2; wire[27:0] t_soft = {s0, 3'b0} + s0; (COEF0==9)

All seven coefficient sets of my_fir are below 258 and all sums fit the 28-bit dout (largest 673*65535 = 4.4e7 < 2^28), so the regrouping is bit-exact; this part is already confirmed by the reference simulation of the kept candidate.

Part B - fltr_compute_* (new)

Each fltr_compute_* module is

q_i <= d_i * C_i                                  (stage 1)
d_out_tmp <= sum of sign_extend20(q_i)            (stage 2, six adder levels)
dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3]                           (stage 3, wires only)

with C7==C1, C6==C2, C5==C3 in all seven modules, so the 7 products are 4 distinct products of the pre-sums s1=d1+d7, s2=d2+d6, s3=d3+d5 and the centre tap d4.

Two facts make the regrouping exact:

  1. Each q_i is 17 bits and no product of this design overflows 17 bits (largest is 255*364 = 92820), and the true sum S = sum_i(d_i*C_i) never reaches 2^20 (largest module total 510*563 = 287130 for f3), so S may be formed at 20 bits with no wrap, and the pair products (d1+d7)*C1 etc. are exact.
  2. The source sign-extends each unsigned q_i by replicating q_i[16] into bits 19:17, which is worth -2^17*q_i[16] modulo 2^20. So the register the source writes is d_out_tmp = S - 2^17*B (mod 2^20), with B = sum_i q_i[16]. q_i[16] can only be 1 when 255*C_i >= 65536, i.e. C_i >= 258; that happens for exactly three coefficients in the whole design: f1's C4=277 (set iff d4 >= 237), f3's C3=C5=364 (set iff d3 >= 181, resp. d5 >= 181), h4's C4=324 (set iff d4 >= 203). f2, h1, h2, h3 have B == 0 identically and need no correction.

So the rewrite stores the uncorrected S in d_out_tmp and applies the -2^17*B correction in stage 3, which in the source carries no logic at all: since the correction touches only bits 19:17, dout = {(d_out_tmp[19:17] - B)[1:0], d_out_tmp[16:3]}. B is carried alongside S by registering the threshold comparisons in stage 1 and a 2-bit count in stage 2, so it arrives with d_out_tmp.

Per module, replace the declarations of q1..q7 and the whole always body (keep clk/din/dout and reg[19:0] d_out_tmp; as they are). Template, shown for fltr_compute_f1 (coefficients 29,101,17,277 from lines 859-865):

    reg[8:0] s2;                 // din[47:40] + din[15:8]  (C2 == C6 == 101)
    reg[8:0] s3;                 // din[39:32] + din[23:16] (C3 == C5 == 17)
    reg[7:0] r4;                 // din[31:24]              (C4 == 277)
    reg b4;                      // q4[16] of the source: d4*277 >= 2^16
    reg[1:0] bcnt;               // that bit, aligned with d_out_tmp
    reg[19:0] d_out_tmp;

    wire[63:0] sop0_out;
    wire[63:0] sop1_out;
    comb_sop_2_18 sop0 (.ax({9'b0, s2}), .ay(19'd101), .bx({10'b0, r4}), .by(19'd277), .result(sop0_out));
    comb_sop_2_18 sop1 (.ax({9'b0, s1}), .ay(19'd29),  .bx({9'b0, s3}),  .by(19'd17),  .result(sop1_out));

    // the source sign-extends each unsigned q_i, worth -2^17 per set MSB; only q4 can set it
    wire[2:0] topc = d_out_tmp[19:17] - {1'b0, bcnt};

    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
        s1 <= din[55:48] + din[7:0];
        s2 <= din[47:40] + din[15:8];
        s3 <= din[39:32] + din[23:16];
        r4 <= din[31:24];
        b4 <= (din[31:24] >= 8'd237);
        bcnt <= {1'b0, b4};
        d_out_tmp <= sop0_out[19:0] + sop1_out[19:0];
        dout <= {topc[1:0], d_out_tmp[16:3]};
    end

The other six follow the same shape; only the block operands, the soft term and the correction differ. Always build the soft terms into a single t_soft wire first and add the block output last, so that exactly one adder level sits between a block output and d_out_tmp:

  • fltr_compute_f2 (lines 889-895: 4,42,163,255) and fltr_compute_h2 (lines 992-998, identical coefficients): one block sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd42),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd163)); wire[19:0] t_c4 = {4'b0, r4, 8'b0} - {12'b0, r4}; (255*r4) wire[19:0] t_soft = t_c4 + {9'b0, s1, 2'b0}; (+ 4*s1) d_out_tmp <= sop0_out[19:0] + t_soft; dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3]; (no correction, no bcnt).
  • fltr_compute_f3 (lines 928-934: 20,179,364, centre 0): one block sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd179),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd364)); wire[19:0] t_soft = {7'b0, s1, 4'b0} + {9'b0, s1, 2'b0}; (20*s1); no r4 at all (the source's q4 is din[31:24]*0); correction b3 <= (din[39:32] >= 8'd181); b5 <= (din[23:16] >= 8'd181); bcnt <= b3 + b5; and dout <= {topc[1:0], d_out_tmp[16:3]};
  • fltr_compute_h1 (lines 959-965: 17,25,193, centre 0): sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd25),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd193)); wire[19:0] t_soft = {7'b0, s1, 4'b0} + {11'b0, s1}; (17*s1); no correction, no r4.
  • fltr_compute_h3 (lines 1030-1036: 23,72,147, centre 0): sop0(.ax({9'b0,s1}),.ay(19'd23),.bx({9'b0,s3}),.by(19'd147)); wire[19:0] t_soft = {5'b0, s2, 6'b0} + {8'b0, s2, 3'b0}; (72*s2); no correction, no r4.
  • fltr_compute_h4 (lines 1065-1071: 14,43,80,324): sop0(.ax({9'b0,s2}),.ay(19'd43),.bx({10'b0,r4}),.by(19'd324)); wire[19:0] t_c1 = {7'b0, s1, 4'b0} - {10'b0, s1, 1'b0}; (14*s1) wire[19:0] t_c3 = {5'b0, s3, 6'b0} + {7'b0, s3, 4'b0}; (80*s3) wire[19:0] t_soft = t_c1 + t_c3;; correction b4 <= (din[31:24] >= 8'd203); bcnt <= {1'b0, b4}; and the corrected dout.

Every soft term above is a non-negative shift-add of a registered value, every concatenation is exactly 20 bits, and all sums are below 2^20, so the 20-bit arithmetic is exact rather than merely congruent.

No assumption about the design's inputs is needed: there is no ASSUMES: line.

Visibility and X behaviour

In fltr_compute_*, q1..q7 and d_out_tmp are read only by the sum and by dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3] respectively (checked in all seven modules), so nothing that disappears inside a block is read elsewhere; dout is the only module output. The register count on every path is unchanged (din -> 1 register -> sum -> d_out_tmp -> dout), all fltr registers are unconditional, and the equivalence testbench compares from the first cycle after reset while the filter inputs are still flushing X, so X timing must match: it does, because an X on any din byte makes the source's d_out_tmp X (it sums all seven q_i), and makes s1/s2/s3 X here. For f3/h1/h3, where the rewrite stops reading din[31:24] (the source multiplies it by 0, and x*0 is x in Verilog), din[31:24] comes from buff_out4 while din[23:16], din[15:8], din[7:0] come from fifos further down the same chain, so those bytes are X whenever buff_out4 is - the rewritten module is X on exactly the same cycles.

Blocks, tiles, and what is left in soft logic
  • Blocks added: 48 on the my_fir side (my_fir_f1 two, each of the other six modules one, times 6 instances) plus 48 on the fltr side (fltr_compute_f1 two, each of the other six one, times 6 instances) = 96 blocks, each taking a DSP tile alone.
  • After the rewrite no * operator is left anywhere in the design: every remaining coefficient is realised as a shift-add. So the design uses 96 DSP tiles, against 224 in the baseline and 107 in the kept candidate: 11 tiles fewer than the kept candidate (2.8e6 area), and in exchange the six-level 20-bit adder chain plus the 7x17 product registers of all 42 fltr instances leave the soft fabric, replaced per instance by three 9-bit pre-adds, at most three 20-bit shift-adds, one 20-bit combining add and a 3-bit correction.
  • Candidates converted: all 30 fltr ids and all 31 my_fir ids listed in REGIONS - every product that ends up inside a block.

  • Candidates left, grouped by reason - coefficient is a cheap shift-add, so keeping it in soft logic lets the module finish in one block instead of two; moving any of them into a block would buy a second DSP tile per instance (253779 each, about 9 CLBs) without shortening any stage, because they are off the block path and are absorbed by the slack in front of the final adder:

    • fltr_compute_f2 889$58, 895$64 (C=4, one shift) and 892$61 (C=255 = 256-1); fltr_compute_h2 992$100, 998$106, 995$103 (same coefficients);
    • fltr_compute_f3 928$72, 934$78 (C=20 = 16+4); fltr_compute_h1 959$86, 965$92 (C=17 = 16+1); fltr_compute_h3 1031$115, 1035$119 (C=72 = 64+8);
    • fltr_compute_h4 1065$128, 1071$134 (C=14 = 16-2) and 1067$130, 1069$132 (C=80 = 64+16);
    • my_fir_f2 1542$169, 1548$180, 1545$174 and my_fir_h2 1716$210, 1722$221, 1719$215 (COEF0=4, COEF3=255); my_fir_f3 1602$184, 1607$193 (12 = 8+4); my_fir_h1 1661$197, 1666$206 (15 = 16-1); my_fir_h3 1775$225, 1780$234 and my_fir_h4 1833$238, 1838$247 (9 = 8+1).
    • The fltr centre taps of f3, h1 and h3 (coefficient 0) are not candidates and simply vanish, as they already do in the baseline.
Stages and delay

Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. No block feeds another block; on both sides a block output goes through at most one soft adder level into a register. The block path of a fltr stage 2 is 0.06 (clock-to-output) + 1.42 (register to block) + 2.14 (block) + 0.96 (block into soft logic) + one 20-bit adder level + the wire to the flip-flop, i.e. about 7.0 ns at the medians and about 8.0 ns if every wire and the adder come out at the pessimistic end - at or below the 8.202 ns my_fir stage that this rewrite does not touch, and far below the baseline's 11.6069 ns. The soft terms t_soft are at most two adder levels deep from a register (about 4.1 ns), so they are ready before the block output reaches the final adder and never extend the stage; this is why f1, whose four products would need a five-operand three-level soft tree, gets a second block instead and ends with a single sop0+sop1 level. The correction B is deliberately moved into stage 3, where the source has only wires, so it costs no level in stage 2.

Soft logic leaving a stage: the six-level 20-bit adder chain of every fltr_compute instance leaves stage 2 (replaced by one adder level after the block), and the seven 17-bit product registers leave stage 1 (replaced by three 9-bit pre-adds and at most 10 further bits of register). That stage was not the slowest - the slowest stage is the my_fir sum, 8.202 ns - but it was the same shape as the baseline's critical path (one hard multiply then six adder levels), so shortening it carries no risk of a new critical path. Stage 1 of fltr becomes a register-to-register 9-bit add, roughly 3.8 ns. The my_fir stages are unchanged from the kept candidate, so the period should stay at about 8.2 ns.

Register stages, per converted region, operands to result:

  • fltr_compute_* (all 30 converted ids): before - operand byte to product: 1 stage (q_i); product to sum: 1 stage, the sum lands in d_out_tmp; d_out_tmp to dout: 1 stage; three stages in all. After - operand byte to the registered pre-sum s1/s2/s3/r4: 1 stage; the block forms its two products and their sum combinationally in the next stage and lands in d_out_tmp: 0 stages between products and sum; d_out_tmp to dout: 1 stage; three stages in all, so the latency of dout is unchanged and the pipeline depth of the design is unchanged.
  • my_fir_* (all 31 converted ids): before - 0 register stages between the products and the sum, both in the stage that writes dout. After - unchanged at 0: the pre-add, the block's products and the final sum are all in the stage that writes dout.

No register is added, moved or removed on the my_fir side; on the fltr side the stage-1 registers change shape (q1..q7 become s1,s2,s3[,r4,b]) but stay in the same stage with the same unconditional clocking, and the added b/bcnt bits do not rely on their initial value: they are X exactly when the data they qualify is X.

DESIGN_CHANGE: each of the six fltr groups drives its seven fltr_compute_* instances with one and the same 56-bit din (lines 824-830), so the three 9-bit pre-sums s1,s2,s3 are computed seven times over per group. Hoisting them into the parent and passing the registered pre-sums (plus din, which fltr_compute_f3/h4/f1 still need for their threshold bits) into the children would delete about 126 of the 9-bit adders and their registers, roughly 100 clusters, at the cost of changing the child port lists - a change to the design, not to the rewrite, so it is not part of this plan.

1	// comb_sop_2_18: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx*by, all four operands unsigned
2	// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); each 18x19 product is 37
3	// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
4	// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
5	// Ports: ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every
6	// input reaches result in the same cycle.
7	module comb_sop_2_18 (
8	    input  [17:0] ax,
9	    input  [18:0] ay,
10	    input  [17:0] bx,
11	    input  [18:0] by,
12	    output [63:0] result
13	);
14	
15	    wire [36:0] prod_a = ax * ay;                                    // 18x19 -> 37, exact
16	    wire [36:0] prod_b = bx * by;                                    // 18x19 -> 37, exact
17	    wire [63:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b;                            // zero-extended, exact
18	
19	    assign result = sum;
20	
21	endmodule

Task

You are the planner. Read the design source, stereovision2.v, and decide which of the candidate arithmetic regions listed below to rewrite onto the hard block described next, or that none should be rewritten. Write a plan for the editor, who carries it out; do not edit any file.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: comb_sop_2_18 (precision INT19)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx*by
  • input ports: ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19]
  • output ports: result[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and result is valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Cost (guidance: go against it only with a reason in the plan)
  • The clock period is the delay of the slowest stage (the logic between one register and the next). A rewrite that does not touch the slowest stage should not be expected to make the design faster, and should not make another stage slower than it.
  • The block's internal delay is fixed. Soft logic between a block's output and the next register adds to that stage; blocks in series each add their delay plus a wire.
  • Moving or adding registers changes stage lengths and when values arrive.
  • Area falls when soft adders and flip-flops move into blocks.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone. Synthesis may already have placed the design's multiplies on tiles, so a block that only replaces one saves little: count tiles against the baseline.
Objective

Minimize area × delay × wirelength against the baseline. If you expect no rewrite to lower it, output TIER: NONE. Among rewrites that lower it, choose the one that lowers it most.

Output
Tiers
  • T1: The block replaces the region's arithmetic as it stands: the same operations on the same operands, now inside the block.
  • T2: The region's arithmetic is regrouped to fit the block (products regrouped into the block's sums, registers moved), computing the same values.
  • NONE: No rewrite: no candidate can be rewritten correctly.
Header

Write exactly this header, each key at the start of its own line, then the plan:

TIER: <exactly one of T1, T2, NONE>
REGIONS: <the converted candidate ids, comma-separated; NONE when TIER is NONE>
SHARED_REDUCTION: <the signal or module the converted products are summed in; NONE for a single region>
BLOCKS: <how many blocks the rewrite instantiates, one integer>
TILES: <how many DSP tiles the whole design then uses, one integer>
STAGE_NS: <the delay of the slowest stage the rewrite leaves, in ns, one number>
MAPPING: <which design signals go to which block ports>
PLAN: <the plan, stating everything listed below>

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output rules
  • Write nothing before the TIER line; read the source first.
  • A reviewer checks the plan automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.
  • If a change to the design itself, not to the rewrite, would let more of it use the block, you may say so on a line starting DESIGN_CHANGE:. It is reported to the user and does not change your decision.
