PLAN:

What changes against the kept candidate

The kept candidate (revision 3) already puts 96 blocks on 96 tiles and turns every remaining multiply into shift-adds, so no hard multiplier is left on a tile. Its measured critical path shows where the remaining time goes: a soft pre-add in front of a block (1.0 ns wire + 0.292 ns carry) and a 28-bit adder plus a LUT behind it (0.96 + 0.518 + 1.494 + 0.153), around a 2.14 ns block — 8.088 ns in total, of which only 2.14 ns is the block and 0.81 ns is adder logic. This revision keeps the same 96 blocks and the same tile count, and spends a small number of flip-flops to put a register on both sides of every block, so the slowest stage becomes register -> wire -> block -> wire -> register, the floor this architecture allows (0.103 + 1.419 + 2.14 + ~2.25 + 0.019 = 5.93 ns, and ~6.2 ns if the block-to-register wire lands above its median). Everything else — the soft pre-adds, the shift-add coefficient terms, and the final reduction adder — moves into neighbouring stages that have slack.

Two mechanisms:

  1. fltr_compute_\* (3 register stages already: pre-sums -> d_out_tmp -> dout). The final 20-bit reduction adder moves out of the block stage into the dout stage, by splitting d_out_tmp into the two registers pa and pb that hold the two addends. No latency change, no new stage.
  2. my_fir_\* (1 register stage: delay line -> dout). The whole product sum except the COEF0*din term is computed one enabled cycle early on taps shifted by one and held in pipeline registers, so the block sits between the delay line and those registers, and the dout stage is only a 3-addend sum. No latency change (proof below), and n_delay_reg6 becomes dead and is removed, paying back part of the added flip-flops.

Block count, mode and tile count are unchanged at 96, so area moves only by the handful of registers added; the gain is the period.

Correctness of the my_fir retiming

Index enabled edges (new_data_rdy==1) by k; d_k is din at edge k, and the delay line gives n_j = d_{k-j} before edge k. The original computes, at every enabled edge,
dout_k = C0*d_k + C1*d_{k-1} + C2*d_{k-2} + C3*d_{k-3} + C4*d_{k-4} + C5*d_{k-5} + C6*d_{k-6}.
Define a register P loaded at every enabled edge with
P_new = C1*din + C2*n1 + C3*n2 + C4*n3 + C5*n4 + C6*n5,
and at the same edge dout <= P + C0*din (non-blocking, so P is the value loaded at the previous enabled edge). Then dout_k = C1*d_{k-1} + C2*d_{k-2} + C3*d_{k-3} + C4*d_{k-4} + C5*d_{k-5} + C6*d_{k-6} + C0*d_k, identical to the original on every cycle, including when the enable is low (both P and dout hold). Every filter is symmetric (C6==C0, C5==C1, C4==C2 in all seven modules), so
P_new = C1*din + C1*n4 + C2*(n1+n3) + C3*n2 + C0*n5,
and n1+n3 at edge k equals d_{k-1}+d_{k-3}, which is produced one edge earlier by the registered pre-sum rs <= din + n2 under the same enable. So every operand of the block is a register output (n4, rs, and for my_fir_f1 also n2, n5); the only term that still depends on the current din is C1*din (soft, into the Ps register) and C0*din (soft, in the dout stage), and neither feeds a block.

dout_k depends on exactly d_k .. d_{k-6} before and after the rewrite (d_{k-5} through n4, d_{k-6} through n5), so the start-up X-flush is cycle-for-cycle identical to the original; the added registers (Pa, Pb, Ps, rs) are loaded on the first enabled edge and the testbench holds v_nd_s* at 1 through the 8 reset cycles and the 80-cycle lead-in (lines 188-197, 514-520), so they are settled long before anything observable. n_delay_reg6 has no other reader (it appears only in the dout expression) and is deleted. All sums are exact: the largest filter has sum of coefficients 525, and 525*65535 = 34.4e6 < 2^28, so every regrouping is exact in 28-bit unsigned arithmetic and the block's 64-bit result never wraps.

Correctness of the fltr_compute rewrite (unchanged from the kept candidate, plus the split)

Each q_i is an unsigned product sign-extended from 17 to 20 bits, which adds -2**17 per term whose bit 16 is set. Only the terms listed below can set bit 16 (b is an 8-bit input byte):
f1 b*277 >= 65536 iff b >= 237; f3 b*364 iff b >= 181 (two such terms, q3 and q5); h4 b*324 iff b >= 203. In f2, h1, h2, h3 the largest product is 255*255 = 65025 < 65536, so no correction is needed there. The correction is formed from a registered count bcnt and applied to bits 19:17 of the reduction sum, exactly as in the kept candidate; it is read in the dout stage together with the sum, so splitting the sum into pa/pb does not move it.

Keep the module headers, ports, COEF* defines and the output_data_ready logic as they are. All constants below are written as 19'dN on ay/by.

Every candidate, converted or left

Converted (53 ids listed in REGIONS, each in 6 instances).

  • fltr_compute_f1, all 7 products: the three symmetric pairs become s1*29, s2*101, s3*17 and the centre r4*277, filling both blocks exactly.
  • fltr_compute_f2/h2 (890, 891, 893, 894 / 993, 994, 996, 997), f3 (929, 930, 932, 933), h1 (960, 961, 963, 964), h3 (1030, 1032, 1034, 1036), h4 (1066, 1068, 1070): the two most expensive pre-added pairs (or pair plus centre, h4) go in the single block of each module.
  • my_fir_f1 (1488, 1489, 1490, 1491, 1492): C2 and C4 merge into rs*15, C5 becomes n4*101, C3 becomes n2*235, C6 becomes n5*29, across two blocks.
  • my_fir_f2/h2, f3, h1, h3, h4 (three ids each): C2 and C4 merge into rs*C2, C5 becomes n4*C1, in the single block of each module.

Left (soft shift-adds, no DSP tile). Grouped by reason:

  • Cheap coefficient, and it would cost a whole extra tile to absorb. fltr_compute_f2/h2 889, 892, 895 / 992, 995, 998 (×4 and ×255); f3 928, 934 (×20); h1 959, 965 (×17); h3 1031, 1035 (×72); h4 1065, 1067, 1069, 1071 (×14 and ×80). Each is one or two shifts and one adder, 1 or 2 levels from a register, in a stage with ≥1.7 ns slack; a tile costs about 9 CLBs and would buy no period.
  • Term that depends on the current din and therefore must not pass through a block. my_fir 1486, 1487 (f1), 1542, 1543 (f2), 1602, 1603 (f3), 1661, 1662 (h1), 1716, 1717 (h2), 1775, 1776 (h3), 1833, 1834 (h4). C0*din lands in the dout stage and C1*din in the ps register; putting either in a block would put its 1.0 ns + 0.29 ns soft pre-add or a second block wire in front of the 2.14 ns block, which is exactly the 1.29 ns the kept candidate pays on its critical path.
  • Cheap trailing coefficient absorbed into the same soft sum. my_fir 1545 (×255), 1548 (×4), 1607 (×12), 1666 (×15), 1719 (×255), 1722 (×4), 1780 (×9), 1838 (×9). One adder or one shift each, in parallel with the block.
Blocks, tiles, and the longest chain of blocks

96 blocks are instantiated (16 per copy of the filter set, 6 copies: 8 in the fltr_compute modules — two in f1, one in each of f2, f3, h1, h2, h3, h4 — and 8 in the my_fir modules — two in f1, one in each of the others). A block in this mode takes a tile alone and no multiply is left in soft-multiplier form anywhere, so the design uses 96 DSP tiles, against 224 in the baseline and 96 in the kept candidate: the tile count and hence the tile share of the area are unchanged, and the only area movement is the registers described below.

No two blocks are ever in series: within a stage the longest chain of blocks is one block, 2.14 ns. In fltr_compute_f1 and my_fir_f1 the two blocks sit side by side and their results meet one stage later. Against the 11.6069 ns baseline stage, and against the 8.06 ns the kept candidate measures, the new slowest stage is register -> 1.419 ns wire -> block 2.14 ns -> wire to register -> setup, 5.93 ns at the median wire and about 6.2 ns if the block-to-register wire lands in the upper half of its 0.83-2.67 ns range; 6.2 ns is what STAGE_NS states.

What soft logic leaves which stage
  • fltr_compute, block stage (pre-sum registers -> d_out_tmp): the 20-bit reduction adder and, in f1/f3/h4, the top-bit correction leave it; the stage becomes block-to-register only. This is the stage that was tied for slowest in the kept candidate (reg -> block -> adder -> LUT -> reg). It receives nothing new.
  • fltr_compute, output stage (pa/pb -> dout): gains that 20-bit adder and the correction, 2 levels, about 4.2 ns. It held only a bit-select before, so it has the slack.
  • my_fir, block stage (delay line -> pa/pb/ps): loses the soft pre-add that fed the block in the kept candidate (the measured 1.0 ns wire + 0.292 ns carry ahead of the block) and loses the 28-bit reduction adder behind it. It is the slowest stage after the rewrite, at block-to-register only.
  • my_fir, output stage (pa/ps -> dout): gains a 3- or 4-addend sum, 2 levels from the pipeline registers and 2-3 levels from din (shift-add for C0*din, then the merges), about 4.2-5.3 ns — below the block stage.
  • my_fir ps path: the C1*din shift-add plus the C0*n5 and (f2/h2) C3*n2 terms, at most 3 adder levels into the ps register, about 5.3 ns, also below the block stage.

Area cost of the change: per fltr_compute instance one extra 20-bit register (the second reduction addend), per my_fir instance the 28-bit pa (and pb in f1) and 28-bit ps and 17-bit rs, minus the deleted 16-bit n_delay_reg6. ps, rs and the fltr pb register adder outputs and so use the flip-flop already present in the BLE that computes them; only the block-output registers are bare flip-flops. The expected area movement is a few percent against a period cut of roughly a fifth, and the wirelength should not grow: the nets that get longer are the short ones into local flip-flops, while the long block-output nets now end at a register instead of crossing to an adder and back.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region
  • fltr_compute_\* (all converted ids). Before: operand byte register -> product register q_i (1 stage) -> d_out_tmp (2nd) -> dout (3rd); the candidate table's "products registered 1 stage before the sum". After: operand byte register -> pre-sum register s1/s2/s3/r4 (1 stage, the pre-add replacing the product register) -> block, combinational, into pa/pb (2nd stage) -> reduction and bit-select into dout (3rd stage). Three register stages from din to dout before and after; the product is no longer registered on its own, it is formed combinationally between the pre-sum register and the block-output register.
  • my_fir_\* (all converted ids). Before: delay-line register -> product -> 6-deep adder chain -> dout, 1 register stage, "products registered 0 stages before the sum". After: delay-line register (one tap earlier, plus the registered pre-sum rs) -> block -> pa/pb (1st stage) -> 3- or 4-addend sum with C0*din -> dout (2nd stage). The product is computed one enabled cycle earlier on taps shifted by one, so the latency from din to dout is still exactly one enabled cycle, as proved above.

DESIGN_CHANGE: fltr_compute_f2 (lines 889-895) and fltr_compute_h2 (lines 992-998) have identical coefficients and, at lines 825 and 828 of every v_fltr_\* module, are fed the identical din, so vidin_out_h2 is always equal to vidin_out_f2; the same holds for my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2 (coefficients 4,42,163,255) and for my_fir_h3 and my_fir_h4 (9,56,109,0) whenever their inputs agree. Deleting the duplicate fltr_compute_h2 instances and driving vidin_out_h2 from the f2 instance would remove 6 filter instances outright — 6 blocks, 6 tiles and all their soft logic — but it is a change to the design rather than to the rewrite, so it is not part of this plan.

5	// Ports: ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Check
  • Every claim the plan makes about the design (who reads a value, a register's reset or enable, widths, cited lines, ASSUMES lines) against the source.
  • That the mapping as described keeps the same behavior.
  • That the plan states everything the planner's output section requires, listed below.

Do not judge cost or style; measurement decides cost.

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output
  • First line exactly APPROVE or REVISE.
  • If REVISE, for each problem: the rule it violates or the required item it omits, by name; the design lines; what to change.
  • Write nothing before the verdict line; read the source first. The verdict is applied automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.

PLAN:

What changes against the kept candidate

The kept candidate (revision 3) already puts 96 blocks on 96 tiles and turns every remaining multiply into shift-adds, so no hard multiplier is left on a tile. Its measured critical path shows where the remaining time goes: a soft pre-add in front of a block (1.0 ns wire + 0.292 ns carry) and a 28-bit adder plus a LUT behind it (0.96 + 0.518 + 1.494 + 0.153), around a 2.14 ns block — 8.088 ns in total, of which only 2.14 ns is the block and 0.81 ns is adder logic. This revision keeps the same 96 blocks and the same tile count, and spends a small number of flip-flops to put a register on both sides of every block, so the slowest stage becomes register -> wire -> block -> wire -> register, the floor this architecture allows (0.103 + 1.419 + 2.14 + ~2.25 + 0.019 = 5.93 ns, and ~6.2 ns if the block-to-register wire lands above its median). Everything else — the soft pre-adds, the shift-add coefficient terms, and the final reduction adder — moves into neighbouring stages that have slack.

Two mechanisms:

  1. fltr_compute_\* (3 register stages already: pre-sums -> d_out_tmp -> dout). The final 20-bit reduction adder moves out of the block stage into the dout stage, by splitting d_out_tmp into the two registers pa and pb that hold the two addends. No latency change, no new stage.
  2. my_fir_\* (1 register stage: delay line -> dout). The whole product sum except the COEF0*din term is computed one enabled cycle early on taps shifted by one and held in pipeline registers, so the block sits between the delay line and those registers, and the dout stage is only a 3-addend sum. No latency change (proof below), and n_delay_reg6 becomes dead and is removed, paying back part of the added flip-flops.

Block count, mode and tile count are unchanged at 96, so area moves only by the handful of registers added; the gain is the period.

Correctness of the my_fir retiming

Index enabled edges (new_data_rdy==1) by k; d_k is din at edge k, and the delay line gives n_j = d_{k-j} before edge k. The original computes, at every enabled edge,
dout_k = C0*d_k + C1*d_{k-1} + C2*d_{k-2} + C3*d_{k-3} + C4*d_{k-4} + C5*d_{k-5} + C6*d_{k-6}.
Define a register P loaded at every enabled edge with
P_new = C1*din + C2*n1 + C3*n2 + C4*n3 + C5*n4 + C6*n5,
and at the same edge dout <= P + C0*din (non-blocking, so P is the value loaded at the previous enabled edge). Then dout_k = C1*d_{k-1} + C2*d_{k-2} + C3*d_{k-3} + C4*d_{k-4} + C5*d_{k-5} + C6*d_{k-6} + C0*d_k, identical to the original on every cycle, including when the enable is low (both P and dout hold). Every filter is symmetric (C6==C0, C5==C1, C4==C2 in all seven modules), so
P_new = C1*din + C1*n4 + C2*(n1+n3) + C3*n2 + C0*n5,
and n1+n3 at edge k equals d_{k-1}+d_{k-3}, which is produced one edge earlier by the registered pre-sum rs <= din + n2 under the same enable. So every operand of the block is a register output (n4, rs, and for my_fir_f1 also n2, n5); the only term that still depends on the current din is C1*din (soft, into the Ps register) and C0*din (soft, in the dout stage), and neither feeds a block.

dout_k depends on exactly d_k .. d_{k-6} before and after the rewrite (d_{k-5} through n4, d_{k-6} through n5), so the start-up X-flush is cycle-for-cycle identical to the original; the added registers (Pa, Pb, Ps, rs) are loaded on the first enabled edge and the testbench holds v_nd_s* at 1 through the 8 reset cycles and the 80-cycle lead-in (lines 188-197, 514-520), so they are settled long before anything observable. n_delay_reg6 has no other reader (it appears only in the dout expression) and is deleted. All sums are exact: the largest filter has sum of coefficients 525, and 525*65535 = 34.4e6 < 2^28, so every regrouping is exact in 28-bit unsigned arithmetic and the block's 64-bit result never wraps.

Correctness of the fltr_compute rewrite (unchanged from the kept candidate, plus the split)

Each q_i is an unsigned product sign-extended from 17 to 20 bits, which adds -2**17 per term whose bit 16 is set. Only the terms listed below can set bit 16 (b is an 8-bit input byte):
f1 b*277 >= 65536 iff b >= 237; f3 b*364 iff b >= 181 (two such terms, q3 and q5); h4 b*324 iff b >= 203. In f2, h1, h2, h3 the largest product is 255*255 = 65025 < 65536, so no correction is needed there. The correction is formed from a registered count bcnt and applied to bits 19:17 of the reduction sum, exactly as in the kept candidate; it is read in the dout stage together with the sum, so splitting the sum into pa/pb does not move it.

Per-module code the editor should produce

Keep the module headers, ports, COEF* defines and the output_data_ready logic as they are. All constants below are written as 19'dN on ay/by.

In every my_fir module n_delay_reg6 is removed (no other reader), rs, pa, ps (and pb in f1) are loaded only inside the if (new_data_rdy) branch, and the parenthesisation above must be kept: it decides the adder depth. All shift terms are written as concatenations so the widths are explicit; the subtractions are all of a larger term minus a smaller one, and 28-bit wrap-around would in any case be the same modulus the original sums in.

Every candidate, converted or left

Converted (53 ids listed in REGIONS, each in 6 instances).

  • fltr_compute_f1, all 7 products: the three symmetric pairs become s1*29, s2*101, s3*17 and the centre r4*277, filling both blocks exactly.
  • fltr_compute_f2/h2 (890, 891, 893, 894 / 993, 994, 996, 997), f3 (929, 930, 932, 933), h1 (960, 961, 963, 964), h3 (1030, 1032, 1034, 1036), h4 (1066, 1068, 1070): the two most expensive pre-added pairs (or pair plus centre, h4) go in the single block of each module.
  • my_fir_f1 (1488, 1489, 1490, 1491, 1492): C2 and C4 merge into rs*15, C5 becomes n4*101, C3 becomes n2*235, C6 becomes n5*29, across two blocks.
  • my_fir_f2/h2, f3, h1, h3, h4 (three ids each): C2 and C4 merge into rs*C2, C5 becomes n4*C1, in the single block of each module.

Left (soft shift-adds, no DSP tile). Grouped by reason:

  • Cheap coefficient, and it would cost a whole extra tile to absorb. fltr_compute_f2/h2 889, 892, 895 / 992, 995, 998 (×4 and ×255); f3 928, 934 (×20); h1 959, 965 (×17); h3 1031, 1035 (×72); h4 1065, 1067, 1069, 1071 (×14 and ×80). Each is one or two shifts and one adder, 1 or 2 levels from a register, in a stage with ≥1.7 ns slack; a tile costs about 9 CLBs and would buy no period.
  • Term that depends on the current din and therefore must not pass through a block. my_fir 1486, 1487 (f1), 1542, 1543 (f2), 1602, 1603 (f3), 1661, 1662 (h1), 1716, 1717 (h2), 1775, 1776 (h3), 1833, 1834 (h4). C0*din lands in the dout stage and C1*din in the ps register; putting either in a block would put its 1.0 ns + 0.29 ns soft pre-add or a second block wire in front of the 2.14 ns block, which is exactly the 1.29 ns the kept candidate pays on its critical path.
  • Cheap trailing coefficient absorbed into the same soft sum. my_fir 1545 (×255), 1548 (×4), 1607 (×12), 1666 (×15), 1719 (×255), 1722 (×4), 1780 (×9), 1838 (×9). One adder or one shift each, in parallel with the block.
Blocks, tiles, and the longest chain of blocks

96 blocks are instantiated (16 per copy of the filter set, 6 copies: 8 in the fltr_compute modules — two in f1, one in each of f2, f3, h1, h2, h3, h4 — and 8 in the my_fir modules — two in f1, one in each of the others). A block in this mode takes a tile alone and no multiply is left in soft-multiplier form anywhere, so the design uses 96 DSP tiles, against 224 in the baseline and 96 in the kept candidate: the tile count and hence the tile share of the area are unchanged, and the only area movement is the registers described below.

No two blocks are ever in series: within a stage the longest chain of blocks is one block, 2.14 ns. In fltr_compute_f1 and my_fir_f1 the two blocks sit side by side and their results meet one stage later. Against the 11.6069 ns baseline stage, and against the 8.06 ns the kept candidate measures, the new slowest stage is register -> 1.419 ns wire -> block 2.14 ns -> wire to register -> setup, 5.93 ns at the median wire and about 6.2 ns if the block-to-register wire lands in the upper half of its 0.83-2.67 ns range; 6.2 ns is what STAGE_NS states.

What soft logic leaves which stage
  • fltr_compute, block stage (pre-sum registers -> d_out_tmp): the 20-bit reduction adder and, in f1/f3/h4, the top-bit correction leave it; the stage becomes block-to-register only. This is the stage that was tied for slowest in the kept candidate (reg -> block -> adder -> LUT -> reg). It receives nothing new.
  • fltr_compute, output stage (pa/pb -> dout): gains that 20-bit adder and the correction, 2 levels, about 4.2 ns. It held only a bit-select before, so it has the slack.
  • my_fir, block stage (delay line -> pa/pb/ps): loses the soft pre-add that fed the block in the kept candidate (the measured 1.0 ns wire + 0.292 ns carry ahead of the block) and loses the 28-bit reduction adder behind it. It is the slowest stage after the rewrite, at block-to-register only.
  • my_fir, output stage (pa/ps -> dout): gains a 3- or 4-addend sum, 2 levels from the pipeline registers and 2-3 levels from din (shift-add for C0*din, then the merges), about 4.2-5.3 ns — below the block stage.
  • my_fir ps path: the C1*din shift-add plus the C0*n5 and (f2/h2) C3*n2 terms, at most 3 adder levels into the ps register, about 5.3 ns, also below the block stage.

Area cost of the change: per fltr_compute instance one extra 20-bit register (the second reduction addend), per my_fir instance the 28-bit pa (and pb in f1) and 28-bit ps and 17-bit rs, minus the deleted 16-bit n_delay_reg6. ps, rs and the fltr pb register adder outputs and so use the flip-flop already present in the BLE that computes them; only the block-output registers are bare flip-flops. The expected area movement is a few percent against a period cut of roughly a fifth, and the wirelength should not grow: the nets that get longer are the short ones into local flip-flops, while the long block-output nets now end at a register instead of crossing to an adder and back.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region
  • fltr_compute_\* (all converted ids). Before: operand byte register -> product register q_i (1 stage) -> d_out_tmp (2nd) -> dout (3rd); the candidate table's "products registered 1 stage before the sum". After: operand byte register -> pre-sum register s1/s2/s3/r4 (1 stage, the pre-add replacing the product register) -> block, combinational, into pa/pb (2nd stage) -> reduction and bit-select into dout (3rd stage). Three register stages from din to dout before and after; the product is no longer registered on its own, it is formed combinationally between the pre-sum register and the block-output register.
  • my_fir_\* (all converted ids). Before: delay-line register -> product -> 6-deep adder chain -> dout, 1 register stage, "products registered 0 stages before the sum". After: delay-line register (one tap earlier, plus the registered pre-sum rs) -> block -> pa/pb (1st stage) -> 3- or 4-addend sum with C0*din -> dout (2nd stage). The product is computed one enabled cycle earlier on taps shifted by one, so the latency from din to dout is still exactly one enabled cycle, as proved above.

DESIGN_CHANGE: fltr_compute_f2 (lines 889-895) and fltr_compute_h2 (lines 992-998) have identical coefficients and, at lines 825 and 828 of every v_fltr_\* module, are fed the identical din, so vidin_out_h2 is always equal to vidin_out_f2; the same holds for my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2 (coefficients 4,42,163,255) and for my_fir_h3 and my_fir_h4 (9,56,109,0) whenever their inputs agree. Deleting the duplicate fltr_compute_h2 instances and driving vidin_out_h2 from the f2 instance would remove 6 filter instances outright — 6 blocks, 6 tiles and all their soft logic — but it is a change to the design rather than to the rewrite, so it is not part of this plan.

Reference simulation

After the edit, the framework simulates the edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle. A candidate that does not match is not measured. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (comb_sop_2_18.v) are in sim_reference/.

Read these files in this directory: stereovision2.v

Checks performed against stereovision2.v and sim_reference/:

  • Coefficients and symmetry. All seven fltr_compute_* tap sets (lines 859-865, 889-895, 928-934, 959-965, 992-998, 1030-1036, 1065-1071) are symmetric C1=C7, C2=C6, C3=C5, and every hard-coded block constant matches (f1 101/277/29/17, f2+h2 42/163, f3 179/364, h1 25/193, h3 23/147, h4 43/324). The soft shift-add terms reproduce ×4, ×255, ×20, ×17, ×72, ×14, ×80 exactly. All seven my_fir_* coefficient sets (lines 1440-1449, 1500-1506, 1561-1567, 1616-1625, 1675-1681, 1734-1740, 1792-1798) are symmetric and match the block constants and the d*/c* shift-adds, and the testbench's -D overrides (tb line 3) carry the same values.
  • Sign-extension correction. Only products that can reach 2^16 are f1 q4 (≥237), f3 q3/q5 (≥181), h4 q4 (≥203); f2/h2/h1/h3 peak at 255·255 < 65536. topc = dsum[19:17] - bcnt reproduces the −2^17·count mod 2^20 of the original, and bcnt (stage 2) stays aligned with pa/pb (stage 2) after the split. Sums stay under 2^20 (max 171615) and under 2^28 (max 525·65535 = 34.4 M), so no regrouping wraps.
  • my_fir retiming. The derivation holds: rs <= din + n_delay_reg2 equals n1+n3 one enabled edge later, pa/pb/ps are loaded only under new_data_rdy, and dout_k depends on exactly d_k…d_{k-6} before and after, so latency and the start-up X window are unchanged. n_delay_reg6 has no reader outside the deleted dout expression in any of the seven modules. output_data_ready, the delay chain and vidin_out_reg_* sampling (lines 514-520, 523-552) are untouched; reset never reaches these modules (it is used only in the block at lines 201-209), so mid-run resets need no handling.
  • Accounting. 91 candidate rows: 53 converted, 38 left in three reason groups — the lists partition the table exactly. 16 blocks per filter set × 6 instances = 96 blocks, 96 tiles; every port driven, no 0 tie needed. Longest block chain, soft logic moved per stage, and before/after register stages are all stated.
  • The parenthetical "(lines 188-197, 514-520)" points at the design's h_fltr/my_fir instantiations rather than the testbench; the fact it supports (strobes idle at 1 through the 8 reset cycles and 80-cycle lead-in) is in tb_equiv_sv2_top.v lines 210-228 and 284-290 and is correct, and the X-flush argument does not depend on it.

1	// comb_sop_2_18: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx*by, all four operands unsigned
2	// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); each 18x19 product is 37
3	// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
4	// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
5	// Ports: ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every
6	// input reaches result in the same cycle.
7	module comb_sop_2_18 (
8	    input  [17:0] ax,
9	    input  [18:0] ay,
10	    input  [17:0] bx,
11	    input  [18:0] by,
12	    output [63:0] result
13	);
14	
15	    wire [36:0] prod_a = ax * ay;                                    // 18x19 -> 37, exact
16	    wire [36:0] prod_b = bx * by;                                    // 18x19 -> 37, exact
17	    wire [63:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b;                            // zero-extended, exact
18	
19	    assign result = sum;
20	
21	endmodule

Task

Edit stereovision2.v in this directory to carry out the approved plan below: rewrite the regions it names onto the hard block described next. If a step cannot be done as the plan says, stop and say which step and why; do not improvise a different rewrite.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: comb_sop_2_18 (precision INT19)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx*by
  • input ports: ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19]
  • output ports: result[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and result is valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
How to work
  • After each edit, run bash check.sh stereovision2.v and read its output. If it fails, fix the RTL and run it again.

PLAN:

What changes against the kept candidate

The kept candidate (revision 3) already puts 96 blocks on 96 tiles and turns every remaining multiply into shift-adds, so no hard multiplier is left on a tile. Its measured critical path shows where the remaining time goes: a soft pre-add in front of a block (1.0 ns wire + 0.292 ns carry) and a 28-bit adder plus a LUT behind it (0.96 + 0.518 + 1.494 + 0.153), around a 2.14 ns block — 8.088 ns in total, of which only 2.14 ns is the block and 0.81 ns is adder logic. This revision keeps the same 96 blocks and the same tile count, and spends a small number of flip-flops to put a register on both sides of every block, so the slowest stage becomes register -> wire -> block -> wire -> register, the floor this architecture allows (0.103 + 1.419 + 2.14 + ~2.25 + 0.019 = 5.93 ns, and ~6.2 ns if the block-to-register wire lands above its median). Everything else — the soft pre-adds, the shift-add coefficient terms, and the final reduction adder — moves into neighbouring stages that have slack.

Two mechanisms:

  1. fltr_compute_\* (3 register stages already: pre-sums -> d_out_tmp -> dout). The final 20-bit reduction adder moves out of the block stage into the dout stage, by splitting d_out_tmp into the two registers pa and pb that hold the two addends. No latency change, no new stage.
  2. my_fir_\* (1 register stage: delay line -> dout). The whole product sum except the COEF0*din term is computed one enabled cycle early on taps shifted by one and held in pipeline registers, so the block sits between the delay line and those registers, and the dout stage is only a 3-addend sum. No latency change (proof below), and n_delay_reg6 becomes dead and is removed, paying back part of the added flip-flops.

Block count, mode and tile count are unchanged at 96, so area moves only by the handful of registers added; the gain is the period.

Correctness of the my_fir retiming

Index enabled edges (new_data_rdy==1) by k; d_k is din at edge k, and the delay line gives n_j = d_{k-j} before edge k. The original computes, at every enabled edge,
dout_k = C0*d_k + C1*d_{k-1} + C2*d_{k-2} + C3*d_{k-3} + C4*d_{k-4} + C5*d_{k-5} + C6*d_{k-6}.
Define a register P loaded at every enabled edge with
P_new = C1*din + C2*n1 + C3*n2 + C4*n3 + C5*n4 + C6*n5,
and at the same edge dout <= P + C0*din (non-blocking, so P is the value loaded at the previous enabled edge). Then dout_k = C1*d_{k-1} + C2*d_{k-2} + C3*d_{k-3} + C4*d_{k-4} + C5*d_{k-5} + C6*d_{k-6} + C0*d_k, identical to the original on every cycle, including when the enable is low (both P and dout hold). Every filter is symmetric (C6==C0, C5==C1, C4==C2 in all seven modules), so
P_new = C1*din + C1*n4 + C2*(n1+n3) + C3*n2 + C0*n5,
and n1+n3 at edge k equals d_{k-1}+d_{k-3}, which is produced one edge earlier by the registered pre-sum rs <= din + n2 under the same enable. So every operand of the block is a register output (n4, rs, and for my_fir_f1 also n2, n5); the only term that still depends on the current din is C1*din (soft, into the Ps register) and C0*din (soft, in the dout stage), and neither feeds a block.

dout_k depends on exactly d_k .. d_{k-6} before and after the rewrite (d_{k-5} through n4, d_{k-6} through n5), so the start-up X-flush is cycle-for-cycle identical to the original; the added registers (Pa, Pb, Ps, rs) are loaded on the first enabled edge and the testbench holds v_nd_s* at 1 through the 8 reset cycles and the 80-cycle lead-in (lines 188-197, 514-520), so they are settled long before anything observable. n_delay_reg6 has no other reader (it appears only in the dout expression) and is deleted. All sums are exact: the largest filter has sum of coefficients 525, and 525*65535 = 34.4e6 < 2^28, so every regrouping is exact in 28-bit unsigned arithmetic and the block's 64-bit result never wraps.

Correctness of the fltr_compute rewrite (unchanged from the kept candidate, plus the split)

Each q_i is an unsigned product sign-extended from 17 to 20 bits, which adds -2**17 per term whose bit 16 is set. Only the terms listed below can set bit 16 (b is an 8-bit input byte):
f1 b*277 >= 65536 iff b >= 237; f3 b*364 iff b >= 181 (two such terms, q3 and q5); h4 b*324 iff b >= 203. In f2, h1, h2, h3 the largest product is 255*255 = 65025 < 65536, so no correction is needed there. The correction is formed from a registered count bcnt and applied to bits 19:17 of the reduction sum, exactly as in the kept candidate; it is read in the dout stage together with the sum, so splitting the sum into pa/pb does not move it.

Keep the module headers, ports, COEF* defines and the output_data_ready logic as they are. All constants below are written as 19'dN on ay/by.

In every my_fir module n_delay_reg6 is removed (no other reader), rs, pa, ps (and pb in f1) are loaded only inside the if (new_data_rdy) branch, and the parenthesisation above must be kept: it decides the adder depth. All shift terms are written as concatenations so the widths are explicit; the subtractions are all of a larger term minus a smaller one, and 28-bit wrap-around would in any case be the same modulus the original sums in.

Every candidate, converted or left

Converted (53 ids listed in REGIONS, each in 6 instances).

  • fltr_compute_f1, all 7 products: the three symmetric pairs become s1*29, s2*101, s3*17 and the centre r4*277, filling both blocks exactly.
  • fltr_compute_f2/h2 (890, 891, 893, 894 / 993, 994, 996, 997), f3 (929, 930, 932, 933), h1 (960, 961, 963, 964), h3 (1030, 1032, 1034, 1036), h4 (1066, 1068, 1070): the two most expensive pre-added pairs (or pair plus centre, h4) go in the single block of each module.
  • my_fir_f1 (1488, 1489, 1490, 1491, 1492): C2 and C4 merge into rs*15, C5 becomes n4*101, C3 becomes n2*235, C6 becomes n5*29, across two blocks.
  • my_fir_f2/h2, f3, h1, h3, h4 (three ids each): C2 and C4 merge into rs*C2, C5 becomes n4*C1, in the single block of each module.

Left (soft shift-adds, no DSP tile). Grouped by reason:

  • Cheap coefficient, and it would cost a whole extra tile to absorb. fltr_compute_f2/h2 889, 892, 895 / 992, 995, 998 (×4 and ×255); f3 928, 934 (×20); h1 959, 965 (×17); h3 1031, 1035 (×72); h4 1065, 1067, 1069, 1071 (×14 and ×80). Each is one or two shifts and one adder, 1 or 2 levels from a register, in a stage with ≥1.7 ns slack; a tile costs about 9 CLBs and would buy no period.
  • Term that depends on the current din and therefore must not pass through a block. my_fir 1486, 1487 (f1), 1542, 1543 (f2), 1602, 1603 (f3), 1661, 1662 (h1), 1716, 1717 (h2), 1775, 1776 (h3), 1833, 1834 (h4). C0*din lands in the dout stage and C1*din in the ps register; putting either in a block would put its 1.0 ns + 0.29 ns soft pre-add or a second block wire in front of the 2.14 ns block, which is exactly the 1.29 ns the kept candidate pays on its critical path.
  • Cheap trailing coefficient absorbed into the same soft sum. my_fir 1545 (×255), 1548 (×4), 1607 (×12), 1666 (×15), 1719 (×255), 1722 (×4), 1780 (×9), 1838 (×9). One adder or one shift each, in parallel with the block.
Blocks, tiles, and the longest chain of blocks

96 blocks are instantiated (16 per copy of the filter set, 6 copies: 8 in the fltr_compute modules — two in f1, one in each of f2, f3, h1, h2, h3, h4 — and 8 in the my_fir modules — two in f1, one in each of the others). A block in this mode takes a tile alone and no multiply is left in soft-multiplier form anywhere, so the design uses 96 DSP tiles, against 224 in the baseline and 96 in the kept candidate: the tile count and hence the tile share of the area are unchanged, and the only area movement is the registers described below.

No two blocks are ever in series: within a stage the longest chain of blocks is one block, 2.14 ns. In fltr_compute_f1 and my_fir_f1 the two blocks sit side by side and their results meet one stage later. Against the 11.6069 ns baseline stage, and against the 8.06 ns the kept candidate measures, the new slowest stage is register -> 1.419 ns wire -> block 2.14 ns -> wire to register -> setup, 5.93 ns at the median wire and about 6.2 ns if the block-to-register wire lands in the upper half of its 0.83-2.67 ns range; 6.2 ns is what STAGE_NS states.

What soft logic leaves which stage
  • fltr_compute, block stage (pre-sum registers -> d_out_tmp): the 20-bit reduction adder and, in f1/f3/h4, the top-bit correction leave it; the stage becomes block-to-register only. This is the stage that was tied for slowest in the kept candidate (reg -> block -> adder -> LUT -> reg). It receives nothing new.
  • fltr_compute, output stage (pa/pb -> dout): gains that 20-bit adder and the correction, 2 levels, about 4.2 ns. It held only a bit-select before, so it has the slack.
  • my_fir, block stage (delay line -> pa/pb/ps): loses the soft pre-add that fed the block in the kept candidate (the measured 1.0 ns wire + 0.292 ns carry ahead of the block) and loses the 28-bit reduction adder behind it. It is the slowest stage after the rewrite, at block-to-register only.
  • my_fir, output stage (pa/ps -> dout): gains a 3- or 4-addend sum, 2 levels from the pipeline registers and 2-3 levels from din (shift-add for C0*din, then the merges), about 4.2-5.3 ns — below the block stage.
  • my_fir ps path: the C1*din shift-add plus the C0*n5 and (f2/h2) C3*n2 terms, at most 3 adder levels into the ps register, about 5.3 ns, also below the block stage.

Area cost of the change: per fltr_compute instance one extra 20-bit register (the second reduction addend), per my_fir instance the 28-bit pa (and pb in f1) and 28-bit ps and 17-bit rs, minus the deleted 16-bit n_delay_reg6. ps, rs and the fltr pb register adder outputs and so use the flip-flop already present in the BLE that computes them; only the block-output registers are bare flip-flops. The expected area movement is a few percent against a period cut of roughly a fifth, and the wirelength should not grow: the nets that get longer are the short ones into local flip-flops, while the long block-output nets now end at a register instead of crossing to an adder and back.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region
  • fltr_compute_\* (all converted ids). Before: operand byte register -> product register q_i (1 stage) -> d_out_tmp (2nd) -> dout (3rd); the candidate table's "products registered 1 stage before the sum". After: operand byte register -> pre-sum register s1/s2/s3/r4 (1 stage, the pre-add replacing the product register) -> block, combinational, into pa/pb (2nd stage) -> reduction and bit-select into dout (3rd stage). Three register stages from din to dout before and after; the product is no longer registered on its own, it is formed combinationally between the pre-sum register and the block-output register.
  • my_fir_\* (all converted ids). Before: delay-line register -> product -> 6-deep adder chain -> dout, 1 register stage, "products registered 0 stages before the sum". After: delay-line register (one tap earlier, plus the registered pre-sum rs) -> block -> pa/pb (1st stage) -> 3- or 4-addend sum with C0*din -> dout (2nd stage). The product is computed one enabled cycle earlier on taps shifted by one, so the latency from din to dout is still exactly one enabled cycle, as proved above.
Simulation

When you finish, the framework simulates your edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle, on its own copy. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (comb_sop_2_18.v) are in sim_reference/; you may read them, but editing them has no effect on the result.

What I changed

fltr_compute_* (7 modules, 8 blocks per copy of the filter set). In each, the seven per-byte product registers q1..q7 and the 20-bit d_out_tmp reduction were replaced by registered symmetric pre-sums s1 = din[55:48]+din[7:0], s2 = din[47:40]+din[15:8], s3 = din[39:32]+din[23:16], r4 = din[31:24], two block-output registers pa/pb, and the reduction dsum = pa + pb moved into the dout stage. Three register stages from din to dout, as before.

  • f1 (859-865 $44..$50): two blocks — s2*101 + r4*277 and s1*29 + s3*17.
  • f2 (890,891,893,894) and h2 (993,994,996,997): one block, s2*42 + s3*163; r4*255 and s1*4 stay soft.
  • f3 (929,930,932,933): one block, s2*179 + s3*364; s1*20 soft.
  • h1 (960,961,963,964): one block, s2*25 + s3*193; s1*17 soft.
  • h3 (1030,1032,1034,1036): one block, s1*23 + s3*147; s2*72 soft.
  • h4 (1066,1068,1070): one block, s2*43 + r4*324; s1*14 and s3*80 soft.

The source sign-extends each unsigned 17-bit product to 20 bits, which is worth -2**17 per term with bit 16 set. In f1, f3 and h4 the wide centre/pair coefficients can set it, so a registered count bcnt (din[31:24]>=237 for f1, din[39:32]>=181 and din[23:16]>=181 for f3, din[31:24]>=203 for h4) is subtracted from dsum[19:17] and dout <= {topc[1:0], dsum[16:3]}. In f2/h2/h1/h3 the largest product is 255*255 < 2**16, so no correction is needed and dout <= dsum[18:3].

my_fir_* (7 modules, 8 blocks per copy). Every term but COEF0*din is now formed one enabled cycle early on taps shifted by one, held in pa (pb in f1) and ps, so the block sits directly between the delay line and a register. Using the symmetry C6==C0, C5==C1, C4==C2, the early sum is C1*din + C2*(n1+n3) + C3*n2 + C1*n4 + C0*n5, with n1+n3 supplied by the registered pre-sum rs <= din + n_delay_reg2. dout <= (held sum) + C0*din keeps the latency at exactly one enabled cycle. n_delay_reg6 had no other reader and was removed.

  • f1 (1488-1492): two blocks — n4*101 + rs*15 and n2*235 + n5*29; 101*din into ps, 29*din soft in the dout stage.
  • f2 (1544,1546,1547) and h2 (1718,1720,1721): one block, n4*42 + rs*163; 42*din + 4*n5 + 255*n2 into ps, 4*din soft.
  • f3 (1604,1605,1606): one block, n4*77 + rs*148; 77*din + 12*n5 into ps, 12*din soft.
  • h1 (1663,1664,1665): one block, n4*25 + rs*193; 25*din + 15*n5 into ps, 15*din soft.
  • h3 (1777,1778,1779) and h4 (1835,1836,1837): one block, n4*56 + rs*109; 56*din + 9*n5 into ps, 9*din soft.

Every block port is driven by name; both product terms are used on all 96 instances, so no port is tied to 0. All operands are zero-extended to the port width and every sum is well inside 28 bits (largest filter: 525*65535 = 34.4e6 < 2**28) and 20 bits for the fltr path, so nothing wraps.

No ASSUMES: — the rewrite is unconditionally equivalent.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Inner-loop check: the front end of the real flow, then a cell census. NOT place-and-route.
# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
# Reads, in the flow's order: blocks.vlib (every hard block of the architecture, declared from its
# models), primitives.vlib (the flow's library of memories, adders and multipliers), then the design;
# then elaborates with the flow's hierarchy check. A module that is not defined, a port name the
# block does not have, or a misspelled block name fails here as it would in the flow. Do not
# declare the target block in the design: blocks.vlib declares it, and a design that defines a module
# of the target block's name fails this check.
# Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole design (the last "Number of cells"
# table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub, registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as
# $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated module by name, which is where a hard-block
# instantiation shows up with its instance count.
set -u
f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
lib=""
[ -f "$here/blocks.vlib" ] && lib="read_verilog -lib $here/blocks.vlib; "
[ -f "$here/primitives.vlib" ] && lib="${lib}read_verilog -nomem2reg $here/primitives.vlib; "
target="$(sed -n 's|^// target block: *\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*\).*|\1|p' "$here/blocks.vlib" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
if [ -n "$target" ] && grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*module[[:space:]]+$target([^A-Za-z0-9_$]|$)" "$f"; then
  echo "FAIL: $f defines module $target; blocks.vlib declares it. Remove the module definition and keep the instances."
  exit 1
fi
out="$(yosys -p "${lib}read_verilog -sv -nolatches $f; hierarchy -check -auto-top -purge_lib; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
  echo "$out" | tail -10
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
                   on {on=0}
                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true

// comb_sop_2_18: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx*by, all four operands unsigned
// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); each 18x19 product is 37
// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
// Ports: ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every
// input reaches result in the same cycle.
module comb_sop_2_18 (
    input  [17:0] ax,
    input  [18:0] ay,
    input  [17:0] bx,
    input  [18:0] by,
    output [63:0] result
);

    wire [36:0] prod_a = ax * ay;                                    // 18x19 -> 37, exact
    wire [36:0] prod_b = bx * by;                                    // 18x19 -> 37, exact
    wire [63:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b;                            // zero-extended, exact

    assign result = sum;

endmodule

        // stereovision2's top (from the generated testbench of 2026-10-16). The six filter streams are
        // v_nd_s*_*_2to0 (strobe) and v_d_reg_s*_*_2to0 (byte); reset is active low. Under START_ONLY
        // the mid-run reset pulses are left out.
        phase = "rst-pattern";   // a reset pattern while data flows: one-cycle, three-cycle and back-to-back pulses
        for (i = 0; i < 120; i = i + 1) begin
            tick;
            vidin_new_data = i[0]; vidin_rgb_reg = i * 7; vidin_addr_reg = i * 131; svid_comp_switch = i[2]; offchip_sram_data_in = {i, ~i};
            reset = (`MIDRUN_RESETS && (i == 10 || (i >= 30 && i < 33) || i == 50 || i == 51 || i == 70 || (i >= 90 && i < 98))) ? 1'b0 : 1'b1;
            {v_nd_s1_left_2to0, v_nd_s2_left_2to0, v_nd_s4_left_2to0, v_nd_s1_right_2to0, v_nd_s2_right_2to0, v_nd_s4_right_2to0} = (i % 3 == 0) ? 6'h3F : {i[0], i[1], i[2], i[0], i[1], i[2]};
            v_d_reg_s1_left_2to0 = i * 3; v_d_reg_s2_left_2to0 = i * 5; v_d_reg_s4_left_2to0 = 255 - i; v_d_reg_s1_right_2to0 = i * 11; v_d_reg_s2_right_2to0 = i * 13; v_d_reg_s4_right_2to0 = 128 + i;
        end
        phase = "max";
        for (i = 0; i < 40; i = i + 1) begin tick; set_zero; reset = 1; {v_d_reg_s1_left_2to0, v_d_reg_s2_left_2to0, v_d_reg_s4_left_2to0, v_d_reg_s1_right_2to0, v_d_reg_s2_right_2to0, v_d_reg_s4_right_2to0} = {6{8'd255}}; end
        phase = "alt";
        for (i = 0; i < 40; i = i + 1) begin tick; set_zero; reset = 1; {v_d_reg_s1_left_2to0, v_d_reg_s2_left_2to0, v_d_reg_s4_left_2to0, v_d_reg_s1_right_2to0, v_d_reg_s2_right_2to0, v_d_reg_s4_right_2to0} = i[0] ? {6{8'd255}} : 48'd0; end
        phase = "ramp";
        for (i = 0; i < 64; i = i + 1) begin tick; set_zero; reset = 1; {v_d_reg_s1_left_2to0, v_d_reg_s2_left_2to0, v_d_reg_s4_left_2to0, v_d_reg_s1_right_2to0, v_d_reg_s2_right_2to0, v_d_reg_s4_right_2to0} = {6{i[7:0] * 8'd4}}; end
        zero_cycles(8);
        // the long random stretch: every data input random, the s1_left strobe every 8 to 12 cycles
        // (port_bus_2to1 shows all six streams only when its counter runs a full round between s1_left
        // strobes), the other five strobes random with probability 1/2, reset 1 in 128
        phase = "random"; gap = 0;
        for (i = 0; i < `RANDOM_CYCLES; i = i + 1) begin
            tick; set_data;
            if (gap == 0) begin draw; gap = 8 + (r32 % 5); end
            gap = gap - 1;
            v_nd_s1_left_2to0 = (gap == 0);
            draw; reset = (`MIDRUN_RESETS && (r32 % 128) == 0) ? 1'b0 : 1'b1;
        end
    integer gap;   // drive_sv2_top.vh: cycles until the next s1_left strobe

{
 "file_path": "/work/simwork/mkref.py",
 "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n# Build a _ref copy of the design: rename every module it defines, and every\n# instantiation of those modules, with a _ref suffix.\nimport re, sys\n\nsrc = open(sys.argv[1]).read()\nnames = re.findall(r'^\\s*module\\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)', src, re.M)\nout = src\nfor n in names:\n    out = re.sub(r'\\b%s\\b' % re.escape(n), n + '_ref', out)\nopen(sys.argv[2], 'w').write(out)\nprint(' '.join(names))\n"
}

fltr_compute_f2_ref b2(clk, din, f2r);\n    fltr_compute_f3 a3(clk, din, f3); fltr_compute_f3_ref b3(clk, din, f3r);\n    fltr_compute_h1 a4(clk, din, h1); fltr_compute_h1_ref b4(clk, din, h1r);\n    fltr_compute_h2 a5(clk, din, h2); fltr_compute_h2_ref b5(clk, din, h2r);\n    fltr_compute_h3 a6(clk, din, h3); fltr_compute_h3_ref b6(clk, din, h3r);\n    fltr_compute_h4 a7(clk, din, h4); fltr_compute_h4_ref b7(clk, din, h4r);\n\n    integer i, j, bad = 0, chk = 0, corr = 0;\n    reg [31:0] p = 32'h1234567;\n    function [7:0] byt; input integer k; begin\n        p = p ^ (p << 13); p = p ^ (p >> 17); p = p ^ (p << 5);\n        case (p % 5)\n            0: byt = 8'd255;\n            1: byt = 8'd237 - (p[1:0]);\n            2: byt = 8'd181 + (p[1:0]) - 2;\n            3: byt = 8'd203 + (p[1:0]) - 2;\n            default: byt = p[7:0];\n        endcase\n    end endfunction\n\n    task cmpall; begin\n        chk = chk + 1;\n        if (f1 !== f1r) begin bad = bad + 1; $display(\"f1 %h %h\", f1r, f1); end\n        if (f2 !== f2r) begin bad = bad + 1; $display(\"f2 %h %h\", f2r, f2); end\n        if (f3 !== f3r) begin bad = bad + 1; PLAN:

What changes against the kept candidate

The kept candidate (revision 3) already puts 96 blocks on 96 tiles and turns every remaining multiply into shift-adds, so no hard multiplier is left on a tile. Its measured critical path shows where the remaining time goes: a soft pre-add in front of a block (1.0 ns wire + 0.292 ns carry) and a 28-bit adder plus a LUT behind it (0.96 + 0.518 + 1.494 + 0.153), around a 2.14 ns block — 8.088 ns in total, of which only 2.14 ns is the block and 0.81 ns is adder logic. This revision keeps the same 96 blocks and the same tile count, and spends a small number of flip-flops to put a register on both sides of every block, so the slowest stage becomes register -> wire -> block -> wire -> register, the floor this architecture allows (0.103 + 1.419 + 2.14 + ~2.25 + 0.019 = 5.93 ns, and ~6.2 ns if the block-to-register wire lands above its median). Everything else — the soft pre-adds, the shift-add coefficient terms, and the final reduction adder — moves into neighbouring stages that have slack.

Two mechanisms:

  1. fltr_compute_\* (3 register stages already: pre-sums -> d_out_tmp -> dout). The final 20-bit reduction adder moves out of the block stage into the dout stage, by splitting d_out_tmp into the two registers pa and pb that hold the two addends. No latency change, no new stage.
  2. my_fir_\* (1 register stage: delay line -> dout). The whole product sum except the COEF0*din term is computed one enabled cycle early on taps shifted by one and held in pipeline registers, so the block sits between the delay line and those registers, and the dout stage is only a 3-addend sum. No latency change (proof below), and n_delay_reg6 becomes dead and is removed, paying back part of the added flip-flops.

Block count, mode and tile count are unchanged at 96, so area moves only by the handful of registers added; the gain is the period.

Correctness of the my_fir retiming

Index enabled edges (new_data_rdy==1) by k; d_k is din at edge k, and the delay line gives n_j = d_{k-j} before edge k. The original computes, at every enabled edge,
dout_k = C0*d_k + C1*d_{k-1} + C2*d_{k-2} + C3*d_{k-3} + C4*d_{k-4} + C5*d_{k-5} + C6*d_{k-6}.
Define a register P loaded at every enabled edge with
P_new = C1*din + C2*n1 + C3*n2 + C4*n3 + C5*n4 + C6*n5,
and at the same edge dout <= P + C0*din (non-blocking, so P is the value loaded at the previous enabled edge). Then dout_k = C1*d_{k-1} + C2*d_{k-2} + C3*d_{k-3} + C4*d_{k-4} + C5*d_{k-5} + C6*d_{k-6} + C0*d_k, identical to the original on every cycle, including when the enable is low (both P and dout hold). Every filter is symmetric (C6==C0, C5==C1, C4==C2 in all seven modules), so
P_new = C1*din + C1*n4 + C2*(n1+n3) + C3*n2 + C0*n5,
and n1+n3 at edge k equals d_{k-1}+d_{k-3}, which is produced one edge earlier by the registered pre-sum rs <= din + n2 under the same enable. So every operand of the block is a register output (n4, rs, and for my_fir_f1 also n2, n5); the only term that still depends on the current din is C1*din (soft, into the Ps register) and C0*din (soft, in the dout stage), and neither feeds a block.

dout_k depends on exactly d_k .. d_{k-6} before and after the rewrite (d_{k-5} through n4, d_{k-6} through n5), so the start-up X-flush is cycle-for-cycle identical to the original; the added registers (Pa, Pb, Ps, rs) are loaded on the first enabled edge and the testbench holds v_nd_s* at 1 through the 8 reset cycles and the 80-cycle lead-in (lines 188-197, 514-520), so they are settled long before anything observable. n_delay_reg6 has no other reader (it appears only in the dout expression) and is deleted. All sums are exact: the largest filter has sum of coefficients 525, and 525*65535 = 34.4e6 < 2^28, so every regrouping is exact in 28-bit unsigned arithmetic and the block's 64-bit result never wraps.

Correctness of the fltr_compute rewrite (unchanged from the kept candidate, plus the split)

Each q_i is an unsigned product sign-extended from 17 to 20 bits, which adds -2**17 per term whose bit 16 is set. Only the terms listed below can set bit 16 (b is an 8-bit input byte):
f1 b*277 >= 65536 iff b >= 237; f3 b*364 iff b >= 181 (two such terms, q3 and q5); h4 b*324 iff b >= 203. In f2, h1, h2, h3 the largest product is 255*255 = 65025 < 65536, so no correction is needed there. The correction is formed from a registered count bcnt and applied to bits 19:17 of the reduction sum, exactly as in the kept candidate; it is read in the dout stage together with the sum, so splitting the sum into pa/pb does not move it.

Keep the module headers, ports, COEF* defines and the output_data_ready logic as they are. All constants below are written as 19'dN on ay/by.

In every my_fir module n_delay_reg6 is removed (no other reader), rs, pa, ps (and pb in f1) are loaded only inside the if (new_data_rdy) branch, and the parenthesisation above must be kept: it decides the adder depth. All shift terms are written as concatenations so the widths are explicit; the subtractions are all of a larger term minus a smaller one, and 28-bit wrap-around would in any case be the same modulus the original sums in.

Every candidate, converted or left

Converted (53 ids listed in REGIONS, each in 6 instances).

  • fltr_compute_f1, all 7 products: the three symmetric pairs become s1*29, s2*101, s3*17 and the centre r4*277, filling both blocks exactly.
  • fltr_compute_f2/h2 (890, 891, 893, 894 / 993, 994, 996, 997), f3 (929, 930, 932, 933), h1 (960, 961, 963, 964), h3 (1030, 1032, 1034, 1036), h4 (1066, 1068, 1070): the two most expensive pre-added pairs (or pair plus centre, h4) go in the single block of each module.
  • my_fir_f1 (1488, 1489, 1490, 1491, 1492): C2 and C4 merge into rs*15, C5 becomes n4*101, C3 becomes n2*235, C6 becomes n5*29, across two blocks.
  • my_fir_f2/h2, f3, h1, h3, h4 (three ids each): C2 and C4 merge into rs*C2, C5 becomes n4*C1, in the single block of each module.

Left (soft shift-adds, no DSP tile). Grouped by reason:

  • Cheap coefficient, and it would cost a whole extra tile to absorb. fltr_compute_f2/h2 889, 892, 895 / 992, 995, 998 (×4 and ×255); f3 928, 934 (×20); h1 959, 965 (×17); h3 1031, 1035 (×72); h4 1065, 1067, 1069, 1071 (×14 and ×80). Each is one or two shifts and one adder, 1 or 2 levels from a register, in a stage with ≥1.7 ns slack; a tile costs about 9 CLBs and would buy no period.
  • Term that depends on the current din and therefore must not pass through a block. my_fir 1486, 1487 (f1), 1542, 1543 (f2), 1602, 1603 (f3), 1661, 1662 (h1), 1716, 1717 (h2), 1775, 1776 (h3), 1833, 1834 (h4). C0*din lands in the dout stage and C1*din in the ps register; putting either in a block would put its 1.0 ns + 0.29 ns soft pre-add or a second block wire in front of the 2.14 ns block, which is exactly the 1.29 ns the kept candidate pays on its critical path.
  • Cheap trailing coefficient absorbed into the same soft sum. my_fir 1545 (×255), 1548 (×4), 1607 (×12), 1666 (×15), 1719 (×255), 1722 (×4), 1780 (×9), 1838 (×9). One adder or one shift each, in parallel with the block.
Blocks, tiles, and the longest chain of blocks

96 blocks are instantiated (16 per copy of the filter set, 6 copies: 8 in the fltr_compute modules — two in f1, one in each of f2, f3, h1, h2, h3, h4 — and 8 in the my_fir modules — two in f1, one in each of the others). A block in this mode takes a tile alone and no multiply is left in soft-multiplier form anywhere, so the design uses 96 DSP tiles, against 224 in the baseline and 96 in the kept candidate: the tile count and hence the tile share of the area are unchanged, and the only area movement is the registers described below.

No two blocks are ever in series: within a stage the longest chain of blocks is one block, 2.14 ns. In fltr_compute_f1 and my_fir_f1 the two blocks sit side by side and their results meet one stage later. Against the 11.6069 ns baseline stage, and against the 8.06 ns the kept candidate measures, the new slowest stage is register -> 1.419 ns wire -> block 2.14 ns -> wire to register -> setup, 5.93 ns at the median wire and about 6.2 ns if the block-to-register wire lands in the upper half of its 0.83-2.67 ns range; 6.2 ns is what STAGE_NS states.

What soft logic leaves which stage
  • fltr_compute, block stage (pre-sum registers -> d_out_tmp): the 20-bit reduction adder and, in f1/f3/h4, the top-bit correction leave it; the stage becomes block-to-register only. This is the stage that was tied for slowest in the kept candidate (reg -> block -> adder -> LUT -> reg). It receives nothing new.
  • fltr_compute, output stage (pa/pb -> dout): gains that 20-bit adder and the correction, 2 levels, about 4.2 ns. It held only a bit-select before, so it has the slack.
  • my_fir, block stage (delay line -> pa/pb/ps): loses the soft pre-add that fed the block in the kept candidate (the measured 1.0 ns wire + 0.292 ns carry ahead of the block) and loses the 28-bit reduction adder behind it. It is the slowest stage after the rewrite, at block-to-register only.
  • my_fir, output stage (pa/ps -> dout): gains a 3- or 4-addend sum, 2 levels from the pipeline registers and 2-3 levels from din (shift-add for C0*din, then the merges), about 4.2-5.3 ns — below the block stage.
  • my_fir ps path: the C1*din shift-add plus the C0*n5 and (f2/h2) C3*n2 terms, at most 3 adder levels into the ps register, about 5.3 ns, also below the block stage.

Area cost of the change: per fltr_compute instance one extra 20-bit register (the second reduction addend), per my_fir instance the 28-bit pa (and pb in f1) and 28-bit ps and 17-bit rs, minus the deleted 16-bit n_delay_reg6. ps, rs and the fltr pb register adder outputs and so use the flip-flop already present in the BLE that computes them; only the block-output registers are bare flip-flops. The expected area movement is a few percent against a period cut of roughly a fifth, and the wirelength should not grow: the nets that get longer are the short ones into local flip-flops, while the long block-output nets now end at a register instead of crossing to an adder and back.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region
  • fltr_compute_\* (all converted ids). Before: operand byte register -> product register q_i (1 stage) -> d_out_tmp (2nd) -> dout (3rd); the candidate table's "products registered 1 stage before the sum". After: operand byte register -> pre-sum register s1/s2/s3/r4 (1 stage, the pre-add replacing the product register) -> block, combinational, into pa/pb (2nd stage) -> reduction and bit-select into dout (3rd stage). Three register stages from din to dout before and after; the product is no longer registered on its own, it is formed combinationally between the pre-sum register and the block-output register.
  • my_fir_\* (all converted ids). Before: delay-line register -> product -> 6-deep adder chain -> dout, 1 register stage, "products registered 0 stages before the sum". After: delay-line register (one tap earlier, plus the registered pre-sum rs) -> block -> pa/pb (1st stage) -> 3- or 4-addend sum with C0*din -> dout (2nd stage). The product is computed one enabled cycle earlier on taps shifted by one, so the latency from din to dout is still exactly one enabled cycle, as proved above.

DESIGN_CHANGE: fltr_compute_f2 (lines 889-895) and fltr_compute_h2 (lines 992-998) have identical coefficients and, at lines 825 and 828 of every v_fltr_\* module, are fed the identical din, so vidin_out_h2 is always equal to vidin_out_f2; the same holds for my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2 (coefficients 4,42,163,255) and for my_fir_h3 and my_fir_h4 (9,56,109,0) whenever their inputs agree. Deleting the duplicate fltr_compute_h2 instances and driving vidin_out_h2 from the f2 instance would remove 6 filter instances outright — 6 blocks, 6 tiles and all their soft logic — but it is a change to the design rather than to the rewrite, so it is not part of this plan.

5	// Ports: ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every

7	module comb_sop_2_18 (
8	    input  [17:0] ax,

18	
19	    assign result = sum;
20	
21	endmodule

layout koios_small · used area 9.73358e+07 · critical path 11.6069 ns · wirelength 436921 · area x delay x wirelength (delay register to register, 2026-10-20) 4.93619e+14 (read from entry; median per term over the entry's seed runs (its seed_medians; seeds lists them))

The objective is area x delay x wirelength (delay register to register, 2026-10-20): VPR's total used logic block area (I/Os and empty grid tiles excluded) times the critical path times the total routed wirelength. Each term is the median over the loop's seeds; the product is the product of the medians. Beside every product stand the ratios against the baseline, A/A0 (area), D/D0 (critical path), W/W0 (wirelength) and their product, so the normalization can be read off. After each measured rewrite, the planner is given every measurement so far and asked for a revision. A revision is built and checked like the first rewrite, and the lowest product is kept, a later rewrite having to beat it by more than 9.41%. The loop stops when the planner declines to revise, when a revision does not lower the best product by more than 9.41%, when a revision fails its checks, or when 9 revisions have been made.

Stated: the BLOCKS, TILES and STAGE_NS lines of the plan header. Measured: the packed DSP tile count from the gate flow, and the median period, area and wirelength over the seeds. "A/A0 · D/D0 · W/W0" are the rewrite's medians over the baseline's, whose product is the "vs baseline" change plus one. "vs previous" is against the rewrite measured before this one. "Path 1 ends in" is read from the rewrite's own timing report and netlist: the constant coefficients on the block (or plain multiply) that path 1 passes through, matched against the constants each module of the edited RTL multiplies by; two modules that share a coefficient set are both named, and the hover text gives the element and its constants. Verification comes from verification.yaml in the run dir when one was written; the loop itself does not run the equivalence checks. Its label is proven when the LEC closed, simulation under assumption when the simulation passed without a closed proof and the plan stated a bound it rests on, simulation only when it stated none; the hover text gives the simulation and LEC results and the stated bounds.
